# Multiple Worlds & Multiple Player Profiles

## Context

Today the game has exactly one world and one implicit player. A single localStorage
key (`minecraft_save_v7`) holds the only world; the player's appearance lives in a
separate global key (`minecraft_skin_v1`). The app boots straight into that one world —
there is no title/menu, no way to keep more than one save, and no notion of distinct
players sharing a browser.

This feature adds **multiple named worlds** and **multiple player profiles**, with the
decided model: **a profile owns its worlds** (1 profile : N worlds), like user accounts
on a shared console. Selecting a profile filters the world list. A profile carries
**name + skin only**; audio settings stay global. Shipped as **one combined feature** on
one branch.

The architecture is well-suited to this: the save layer's `readSave`/`writeSave` already
take a key parameter (always called with the one constant today), the engine is fully
headless and disposable, and the mount lifecycle already tears down everything cleanly on
unmount — so worlds can be switched at runtime via a React `key` remount, with no page
reload and no engine refactor.

Branch: `feat/worlds-and-profiles` off `main`.

## Data model (localStorage)

| Key | Shape | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `minecraft_profiles_v1` | `ProfilesManifest` | profile list + `activeProfileId` |
| `minecraft_worlds_v1` | `WorldsManifest` | world index across all profiles |
| `minecraft_world_save_<worldId>` | `SaveData` (v5, **unchanged**) | one bundled blob per world, via existing `readSave`/`writeSave` |
| `minecraft_audio_v1` | `AudioSettings` | **global, untouched** |
| `minecraft_skin_v1` | `SkinSettings` | legacy — read once during migration, then goes stale |
| `minecraft_save_v7` | `SaveData` | legacy — consumed once during migration |

```ts
// lib/game/profiles.ts
type Profile = { id: string; name: string; skinId: SkinId; createdAt: number };
type ProfilesManifest = { version: 1; profiles: Profile[]; activeProfileId: string | null };

// lib/game/worlds.ts
type WorldMeta = {
  id: string; profileId: string;        // the 1:N link
  name: string; seed: number;
  worldgenVersion: number;              // 7 today (see below)
  createdAt: number; lastPlayedAt: number;
};
type WorldsManifest = { version: 1; worlds: WorldMeta[] };
const WORLD_SAVE_PREFIX = "minecraft_world_save_";
function worldSaveKey(id: string) { return WORLD_SAVE_PREFIX + id; }
```

Both manifests use a `{ version: 1, ... }` envelope so they can migrate later, mirroring
`SaveData.version`. Readers are **total** (never throw): drop malformed entries, coerce
`skinId` via `isSkinId`, and repair `activeProfileId` if it points at a deleted profile.

**Seed:** resolved once at `createWorld(profileId, name, seedInput)` and stored on
`WorldMeta.seed` (the manifest becomes the source of truth). Empty input → random in the
same `Math.floor(Math.random()*2147483647)` range the engine uses today; numeric input →
clamped int; non-numeric text → stable hash (Minecraft-style). A fresh world boots with
`new GameEngine({ seed })`; a returning world with `new GameEngine({ save: readSave(key) })`.

**`worldgenVersion` (do NOT bake `_v7` into the key):** keep the per-world save key
version-free. Store `WORLDGEN_VERSION` (= 7 today, new `config.ts` constant) on each
world. The historical `SAVE_KEY` bumps that invalidated block-diff baselines become a
per-world check: if `world.worldgenVersion !== WORLDGEN_VERSION` at load, discard that
world's blob and reboot from its stored seed. Same semantics as today's `_v7` bump, but
per-world and with no key migration.

## Legacy save migration

New `lib/game/legacyMigration.ts` → `migrateLegacySave(storage = localStorage)`, called
once from the menu shell on first mount. **Idempotent**, gated on the *profiles manifest's
absence* (not the legacy save's presence — survives rollback):

1. If `minecraft_profiles_v1` exists → return (already migrated).
2. Read legacy `minecraft_save_v7` (runs the v1→v5 chain) and `minecraft_skin_v1`.
3. `createProfile("Player", legacySkin)` → becomes active.
4. If a legacy save exists: `createWorld(profile.id, "My World", String(seed))` then
   **copy** the blob to `worldSaveKey(world.id)` (copy, not move — a quota failure can't
   lose data), then `removeItem("minecraft_save_v7")` after the copy succeeds.
5. No legacy save (brand-new player): just the default profile, zero worlds.

Leave `minecraft_skin_v1` in place (harmless; per-profile skin now owns appearance).

## React shell / menu state machine

Split `app/page.tsx` so a new **menu shell** sits *above* `MinecraftGame` — the game
component stays "the running game for one world" and its big lifecycle `useEffect` is
untouched.

- **New `components/GameShell.tsx`** owns the screen machine + active profile/world +
  a `playNonce`, runs `migrateLegacySave()` once, and renders the game subtree.
  ```ts
  type Screen =
    | { name: "profile-select" }
    | { name: "world-select"; profileId: string }
    | { name: "play"; profileId: string; worldId: string };
  ```
  Default landing: `profile-select` (active profile highlighted). Flows: pick profile →
  world-select; pick world → `touchWorld(id)` then play; create/rename/delete profile &
  world stay on their screens; "Back" world→profile.

- **Runtime world switch with NO reload — the `key` trick.** Render play as:
  ```tsx
  <MinecraftGame
    key={`${screen.worldId}:${playNonce}`}   // remounts → effect cleanup disposes old engine/renderer
    worldId={screen.worldId} world={world} profile={activeProfile}
    onQuitToWorlds={...} onReloadWorld={() => setPlayNonce(n => n + 1)}
  />
  ```
  Changing `worldId` (or bumping `playNonce`) unmounts the subtree, which runs the existing
  cleanup in `useMinecraftGame.ts:258-273` (disposes renderer/audio/input, clears rAF +
  autosave interval, removes `beforeunload`). A fresh mount boots the new world. This is
  the central move — **zero engine changes**.

- **New menu components** under `components/menu/`: `ProfileSelect.tsx`,
  `WorldSelect.tsx` (worlds for active profile, sorted by `lastPlayedAt`),
  `CreateProfileForm.tsx` (name + skin swatch grid, reusing `SKIN_PRESETS` /
  `skinPortraitUrl` exactly as `PauseMenu` does), `CreateWorldForm.tsx` (name + optional
  seed). Style with existing tokens (`.mc-button`, `.pause-overlay`); add `.menu-screen`/
  `.profile-card`/`.world-card` to a new `app/menu.css` imported after `ui.css` in
  `app/layout.tsx`. Zero binary assets — portraits use the generated `skinPortraitUrl`.

## Wiring `useMinecraftGame` to the selected world + profile

`useMinecraftGame(opts: { worldId; world: WorldMeta; profile; onQuitToWorlds; onReloadWorld })`,
threaded through `MinecraftGame`. Capture `saveKeyRef = worldSaveKey(opts.worldId)` (stable
for the mount's life). Changes in `lib/game/useMinecraftGame.ts`:

- **`persistGame(api, saveKey, onMessage)`** (currently hardcodes `SAVE_KEY` at line 71) —
  add the key param.
- **`attachMount`** (130): `new GameEngine({ save: readSave(saveKeyRef.current) ?? undefined, seed: opts.world.seed })` — engine prefers `save.seed`, falls back to `seed` for a fresh world.
- **autosave + `beforeunload`** (187-189) and **`saveNow`** (331): use `saveKeyRef.current`.
- **`loadNow`** (334): no reload — guard on `readSave(saveKeyRef.current)`, else call `onReloadWorld()` (nonce bump → remount re-reads disk).
- **`resetNow`** (342): `removeItem(saveKeyRef.current)` then `onReloadWorld()` — fresh mount finds no save, reboots from the stored seed (world keeps its name/seed/identity; this is "Reset World", not delete).
- **Skin from profile**: replace `readSkinSettings()` (100) with `opts.profile.skinId`; `updateSkin` (116) calls `setProfileSkin(opts.profile.id, id)` instead of `writeSkinSettings`, still `setPlayerSkin(...)`.
- **New `quitToWorlds()`**: `persistGame(engine, saveKeyRef.current, flashMessage)` *then* `opts.onQuitToWorlds()` — the autosave interval is cleared on unmount and `beforeunload` doesn't fire on in-app nav, so the quit must save synchronously.
- **Audio unchanged** — stays global.

`components/game/PauseMenu.tsx`: add a **"Quit to Worlds"** button (new `onQuitToWorlds`
prop) next to the existing Save/Load/Reset; skin grid now edits the active profile.

## Files

**New:** `lib/game/manifest.ts` (versioned read/write envelope), `lib/game/profiles.ts`,
`lib/game/worlds.ts`, `lib/game/legacyMigration.ts`, `components/GameShell.tsx`,
`components/menu/{ProfileSelect,WorldSelect,CreateProfileForm,CreateWorldForm}.tsx`,
`app/menu.css`.

**Modified:** `app/page.tsx` (render `GameShell`), `app/layout.tsx` (import menu.css),
`components/MinecraftGame.tsx` (accept/pass props), `lib/game/useMinecraftGame.ts` (above),
`components/game/PauseMenu.tsx` (Quit to Worlds), `lib/game/config.ts`
(`WORLDGEN_VERSION`; mark `SAVE_KEY` as legacy/migration-only).

**Reuse (don't reinvent):** `readSave`/`writeSave` (`lib/game/save.ts:75,92`),
`GameEngine` `{ save, seed }` precedence (`GameEngine.ts:88`), `SKIN_PRESETS` /
`isSkinId` / `skinPortraitUrl` (`playerSkins.ts`), the existing dispose-on-unmount cleanup.

## Edge cases

- **Delete active world:** only reachable from `world-select` (not while playing). On any world delete, also `removeItem(worldSaveKey(id))`.
- **Delete profile with N worlds:** cascade — remove each world's blob + manifest entry *before* removing the profile.
- **Last world / last profile gone:** empty world-select state ("Create your first world"); if zero profiles, route to "create first profile" (`activeProfileId = null`, no profile-less play).
- **Autosave to the right key after a switch:** guaranteed — old interval is cleared in cleanup before the new mount installs its own reading the new `saveKeyRef`.
- **Pointer lock:** menus are plain DOM with no canvas; the "Double-click to play" hint only renders inside `play`; cleanup already runs `exitPointerLock()` so the cursor is free in menus.
- **StrictMode double-mount (dev):** migration is idempotent, so safe.

## Testing & verification

**Unit** (co-located `*.test.ts`, injectable `fakeStorage()` per `skinSettings.test.ts`):
`profiles.test.ts` (CRUD, corrupt-manifest fallback, `activeProfileId` repair),
`worlds.test.ts` (seed resolution: empty/numeric/text-hash/clamp; `worldsForProfile`
filter+sort; `worldSaveKey`; delete), `legacyMigration.test.ts` (all branches +
idempotency + blob copied with matching seed + legacy key removed + audio untouched).

**Component** (`*.test.tsx`): `ProfileSelect`/`WorldSelect`/`CreateWorldForm` (lists,
callbacks, empty states), extend `PauseMenu.test.tsx` (Quit to Worlds fires; add prop to
`renderMenu` defaults), optional `GameShell.test.tsx` with a mocked `MinecraftGame`
asserting the `key` changes on switch.

**E2E** (`e2e/*.e2e.ts`): new `menu.e2e.ts` — fresh storage → profile-select → create
profile → create world (fixed seed) → play, assert `window.__monecraft` boots with that
seed; pause → Quit to Worlds → re-enter, seed persists; create a 2nd world, switch, assert
`__monecraft.engine.state.world.seed` changes **with no page navigation**. Update
`e2e/helpers.ts` to pre-seed a default profile+world via `addInitScript` so existing
gameplay tests still land in play. Update `e2e/smoke.e2e.ts` — its three hardcoded
`minecraft_save_v7` / `minecraft_skin_v1` literals must move to the per-world key /
profile skin.

**Verify gate** (must be green before landing): `bun run lint`, `bun run typecheck`,
`bun run format:check`, `bun test`, `bun run build`; `bun run test:e2e` (renderer/input/
shell touched). Manual pass: create two profiles, create worlds under each, switch worlds
without reload, confirm autosave lands in the right blob, reset a world, delete a world and
a profile, confirm a pre-existing `minecraft_save_v7` migrates into "Player / My World".

**Docs (ship with the change):** `docs/save-format.md` (manifests, per-world key, legacy
migration, `worldgenVersion` discard rule — primary), `docs/architecture.md` (GameShell →
`key` remount lifecycle), `docs/manual.md` + `docs/reference.md` (menus, seed entry),
`docs/testing.md` (e2e boots through menus), `README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`.

## Commit slicing (Conventional Commits; lint/build green each step)

1. `feat(save): add versioned profile + world manifests` — `manifest/profiles/worlds.ts`, `WORLDGEN_VERSION`, unit tests. Pure data layer, app still on legacy save.
2. `feat(save): migrate the legacy single save into a default profile + world` — `legacyMigration.ts` + test, not yet UI-wired.
3. `refactor(game): parameterize useMinecraftGame by world + profile` — thread props, per-world key, skin-from-profile; `app/page.tsx` shim still boots one world; update e2e helpers.
4. `feat(menu): add GameShell state machine and menu screens` — shell + menu components + CSS, `key` remount, Quit to Worlds, `loadNow`/`resetNow` nonce rewrite; component tests.
5. `test(e2e): boot through the menu and cover world switching` — helpers + smoke updates, new `menu.e2e.ts`.
6. `docs: document profiles, worlds, and the save-key model`.

there is no title/menu, no way to keep more than one save, and no notion of distinct
players sharing a browser.

This feature adds **multiple named worlds** and **multiple player profiles**, with the
decided model: **a profile owns its worlds** (1 profile : N worlds), like user accounts
on a shared console. Selecting a profile filters the world list. A profile carries
**name + skin only**; audio settings stay global. Shipped as **one combined feature** on
one branch.

The architecture is well-suited to this: the save layer's `readSave`/`writeSave` already
take a key parameter (always called with the one constant today), the engine is fully
headless and disposable, and the mount lifecycle already tears down everything cleanly on
unmount — so worlds can be switched at runtime via a React `key` remount, with no page
reload and no engine refactor.

Branch: `feat/worlds-and-profiles` off `main`.

| `minecraft_skin_v1` | `SkinSettings` | legacy — read once during migration, then goes stale |

```ts
type Profile = { id: string; name: string; skinId: SkinId; createdAt: number };
type ProfilesManifest = { version: 1; profiles: Profile[]; activeProfileId: string | null };

// lib/game/worlds.ts
type WorldMeta = {
  id: string; profileId: string;        // the 1:N link
  name: string; seed: number;
  worldgenVersion: number;              // 7 today (see below)
  createdAt: number; lastPlayedAt: number;
};
type WorldsManifest = { version: 1; worlds: WorldMeta[] };
const WORLD_SAVE_PREFIX = "minecraft_world_save_";
function worldSaveKey(id: string) { return WORLD_SAVE_PREFIX + id; }
```

`skinId` via `isSkinId`, and repair `activeProfileId` if it points at a deleted profile.

# Multiple Worlds & Multiple Player Profiles

## Context

Today the game has exactly one world and one implicit player. A single localStorage
key (`minecraft_save_v7`) holds the only world; the player's appearance lives in a
separate global key (`minecraft_skin_v1`). The app boots straight into that one world —
there is no title/menu, no way to keep more than one save, and no notion of distinct
players sharing a browser.

This feature adds **multiple named worlds** and **multiple player profiles**, with the
decided model: **a profile owns its worlds** (1 profile : N worlds), like user accounts
on a shared console. Selecting a profile filters the world list. A profile carries
**name + skin only**; audio settings stay global. Shipped as **one combined feature** on
one branch.

The architecture is well-suited to this: the save layer's `readSave`/`writeSave` already
take a key parameter (always called with the one constant today), the engine is fully
headless and disposable, and the mount lifecycle already tears down everything cleanly on
unmount — so worlds can be switched at runtime via a React `key` remount, with no page
reload and no engine refactor.

Branch: `feat/worlds-and-profiles` off `main`.

## Data model (localStorage)

| Key | Shape | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `minecraft_profiles_v1` | `ProfilesManifest` | profile list + `activeProfileId` |
| `minecraft_worlds_v1` | `WorldsManifest` | world index across all profiles |
| `minecraft_world_save_<worldId>` | `SaveData` (v5, **unchanged**) | one bundled blob per world, via existing `readSave`/`writeSave` |
| `minecraft_audio_v1` | `AudioSettings` | **global, untouched** |
| `minecraft_skin_v1` | `SkinSettings` | legacy — read once during migration, then goes stale |
| `minecraft_save_v7` | `SaveData` | legacy — consumed once during migration |

```ts
// lib/game/profiles.ts
type Profile = { id: string; name: string; skinId: SkinId; createdAt: number };
type ProfilesManifest = { version: 1; profiles: Profile[]; activeProfileId: string | null };

// lib/game/worlds.ts
type WorldMeta = {
  id: string; profileId: string;        // the 1:N link
  name: string; seed: number;
  worldgenVersion: number;              // 7 today (see below)
  createdAt: number; lastPlayedAt: number;
};
type WorldsManifest = { version: 1; worlds: WorldMeta[] };
const WORLD_SAVE_PREFIX = "minecraft_world_save_";
function worldSaveKey(id: string) { return WORLD_SAVE_PREFIX + id; }
```

`SaveData.version`. Readers are **total** (never throw): drop malformed entries, coerce

**Seed:** resolved once at `createWorld(profileId, name, seedInput)` and stored on

same `Math.floor(Math.random()*2147483647)` range the engine uses today; numeric input →
clamped int; non-numeric text → stable hash (Minecraft-style). A fresh world boots with
`new GameEngine({ seed })`; a returning world with `new GameEngine({ save: readSave(key) })`.

**`worldgenVersion` (do NOT bake `_v7` into the key):** keep the per-world save key
version-free. Store `WORLDGEN_VERSION` (= 7 today, new `config.ts` constant) on each
world. The historical `SAVE_KEY` bumps that invalidated block-diff baselines become a
per-world check: if `world.worldgenVersion !== WORLDGEN_VERSION` at load, discard that
world's blob and reboot from its stored seed. Same semantics as today's `_v7` bump, but
per-world and with no key migration.

feat(save): add versioned profile and world manifests

Introduce the data layer for multiple worlds and player profiles. Two
versioned localStorage manifests sit above the existing per-world save
blobs:

- profiles.ts: a profile is a player identity (name + skin) that owns a
  list of worlds. Readers are total — malformed entries are dropped, skin
  ids sanitized, and a dangling activeProfileId repaired to a real one.
- worlds.ts: each world records its profileId, name, a seed resolved once
  at creation (blank -> random, numeric -> clamped, text -> stable FNV
  hash), and the WORLDGEN_VERSION it was generated under. The heavy
  SaveData stays in its own minecraft_world_save_<id> key.
- manifest.ts: shared read-guard / swallow-on-write / injectable-deps
  helpers so both modules stay declarative and unit-testable.

config.ts gains WORLDGEN_VERSION (the worldgen baseline, today 7) so a
future baseline bump can discard a single world's stale block-diffs
per-world instead of wiping every save via a SAVE_KEY rename. SAVE_KEY is
now legacy: only the upcoming migration reads it.

Pure data layer with no consumers yet; the app still boots the legacy
single save. Covered by profiles.test.ts and worlds.test.ts.
EOF

feat(save): migrate the legacy single save into a default profile + world

On first boot after the feature lands, fold the old single-world setup
into the new model: a default "Player" profile carrying the legacy global
skin, plus one "My World" pointing at a copy of the legacy save blob.

The migration is idempotent and gated on the profiles manifest being
absent (its presence is the already-ran flag, which survives a rollback
that re-creates the legacy key). The legacy blob is copied — not moved —
to the per-world key and only then is the legacy key removed, so a
mid-migration quota failure can never lose the original. A brand-new
player with no legacy save just gets the default profile and no worlds.

Not wired into the UI yet; the shell will call this on mount in a later
commit. Covered by legacyMigration.test.ts.
EOF

git add -A && git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
refactor(game): drive the game by a selected world and profile

Parameterize useMinecraftGame with the world and profile to play, so one
mounted game is one world owned by one profile. The hook now:

- persists to that world's own minecraft_world_save_<id> key (passed
  through persistGame, autosave, beforeunload, saveNow) instead of the
  single legacy SAVE_KEY;
- boots the engine from the world's stored seed for a fresh world, or its
  saved blob when one exists;
- sources the player skin from the profile (updateSkin writes the profile
  manifest, not the old global skin key); audio stays global;
- replaces the page-reloading Load/Reset with an onReloadWorld remount and
  adds quitToWorlds, which saves synchronously before leaving (the
  autosave interval is gone on unmount and beforeunload won't fire on an
  in-app switch).

PauseMenu gains a "Save & Quit to Worlds" action. A temporary shim in
app/page.tsx runs the legacy migration and boots the active profile's
most-recent world (creating defaults if needed), so the app still drops
straight into one world until the selection menus land. Smoke e2e
assertions follow the data to the new per-world / per-profile keys.
EOF

15	- `blockEntities` (optional) — chest contents as `{ index, slots }[]`, keyed by the block's voxel index (the same index space as `changes`). 16	- `lootedChests` (optional) — voxel indices of dungeon loot chests the player has already opened or broken. Dungeon chests are placed by worldgen, so their contents are **not** in `changes`/`blockEntities` until accessed; the engine fills them lazily on first access (loot seeded from `world.seed ^ index`) and records the index here. Because an emptied chest drops out of `blockEntities`, this set — not the chest's emptiness — is what prevents a re-roll on reload. The session-only set of _which_ indices are dungeon chests/spawners is not stored; it is re-derived from the seed each load via `collectDungeonSites` (`lib/world/generation.ts`). 18	Stored in localStorage under `SAVE_KEY` (`minecraft_save_v7`, defined in `lib/game/config.ts`). 19

21

26	(breath restores to full).

32	- **v5** — adds optional `lootedChests` (opened/broken dungeon loot chests). `migrateSaveV4toV5` is a pure version bump (absent → no dungeon chests yet looted). 33	- **v4** — adds optional `blockEntities` (chest contents). `migrateSaveV3toV4` is a pure version bump (absent → restores as no containers), so **`SAVE_KEY` was unchanged** at the time (player-placed chests only; worldgen and the index formula were untouched) and v1/v2/v3 saves load fine.

38

40	
41	Every 15s via `setInterval`, plus on `beforeunload`.

## Schema

- world `seed`

- equipped armor
- selected hotbar slot (0–8)
- player position

- `spawnPoint` (optional, `{x,y,z}` or null) — the bed respawn point; respawn falls back to a random land point when it is null or the block there is no longer a bed
- `blockEntities` (optional) — chest contents as `{ index, slots }[]`, keyed by the block's voxel index (the same index space as `changes`). Only **non-empty** chests are stored; an empty one carries no data and is recreated empty when opened. On load each entry is kept only if that index still holds a Chest block. This is the first per-block metadata in the format — `lib/game/save.ts` (`serializeContainers` / `readContainers`) handles it
- `lootedChests` (optional) — voxel indices of dungeon loot chests the player has already opened or broken. Dungeon chests are placed by worldgen, so their contents are **not** in `changes`/`blockEntities` until accessed; the engine fills them lazily on first access (loot seeded from `world.seed ^ index`) and records the index here. Because an emptied chest drops out of `blockEntities`, this set — not the chest's emptiness — is what prevents a re-roll on reload. The session-only set of _which_ indices are dungeon chests/spawners is not stored; it is re-derived from the seed each load via `collectDungeonSites` (`lib/world/generation.ts`). Handled by `serializeLootedChests` / `readLootedChests` in `lib/game/save.ts`

Read/write and restore validation live in `lib/game/save.ts` (the `Storage` is injectable for tests); `GameEngine.serialize()` produces the save from live state, and `lib/game/engine/blockChanges.ts` maintains the block diff.

Audio volume preferences live under a **separate** key (`minecraft_audio_v1`, `lib/game/audio/settings.ts`) and are not part of the world save or its versioning.

**Per-voxel light is never serialized.** It is a derived cache (`world.light`), recomputed from the blocks at load by `computeFullLight` and patched locally on every edit (`lib/world/lighting.ts`); the bake reads only `world.blocks`, so the save needs no lighting field.

Continuous-water exposure, lava burn, and the oxygen/drowning meter all live only

(breath restores to full).

### Version history

- **v5** (unchanged for caves & lighting) — the lighting system adds no persisted state (light is a derived cache, recomputed at load), and lava is worldgen, not a saved field. So the save _schema_ stays at version 5. But the deep-cave lava changes the deterministic terrain baseline, so **`SAVE_KEY` is bumped `minecraft_save_v6` → `minecraft_save_v7`**: old block-diffs were computed against the lava-free world and must never be applied to the new one. Pre-lava saves are discarded in practice. Torches are additive items/blocks, persisted by string id / in the block diff like any other placed block.
- **v5** (unchanged for ranged combat & the endgame boss) — bows, arrows, the Cursed Totem, the Dragon Heart, and the Dragon Sword are **additive items**, persisted by string id in the existing inventory/container slots, so no schema change was needed. **Arrows in flight, the boss, its minions, and the `victory` flag are all transient** (never serialized — like mobs), and there is no worldgen change (the boss is summoned, not generated), so neither the `version` nor `SAVE_KEY` moved.
- **v5** — adds optional `lootedChests` (opened/broken dungeon loot chests). `migrateSaveV4toV5` is a pure version bump (absent → no dungeon chests yet looted). Unlike v3/v4, **`SAVE_KEY` is bumped to `minecraft_save_v6`** here — not because of the save _shape_ (the field is additive) but because the dungeon worldgen changed the deterministic terrain baseline, so old block-diffs would index against the wrong world. Pre-dungeon saves are therefore discarded in practice; the migration keeps the version chain complete regardless. `readSave` chains v1 → v2 → v3 → v4 → v5.
- **v4** — adds optional `blockEntities` (chest contents). `migrateSaveV3toV4` is a pure version bump (absent → restores as no containers), so **`SAVE_KEY` was unchanged** at the time (player-placed chests only; worldgen and the index formula were untouched) and v1/v2/v3 saves load fine.
- **v3** — adds optional `dayClock`, `hearts`, `hunger`, and `spawnPoint`. `migrateSaveV2toV3` is a pure version bump (the new fields stay absent and restore as engine defaults), so **`SAVE_KEY` is unchanged** and v1/v2 saves load fine.
- **v2** — same fields as v1, reinterpreted for the 36-slot inventory and 9-slot hotbar.
- **v1** — 40 slots, 10-slot hotbar. Still accepted: `readSave` runs `migrateSaveV1toV2`, which packs non-empty slots in order, merges stackable items into earlier stacks, clamps `selectedSlot` to 0–8, and drops items that overflow the smaller inventory.
- Unknown future versions are rejected (treated as no save).

## Autosave

Every 15s via `setInterval`, plus on `beforeunload`.

## Compatibility rules

- Saves store **diffs against generated terrain**, so changing world generation or the voxel index formula (`x + z*sizeX + y*sizeX*sizeZ`) silently corrupts existing saves — bump `SAVE_KEY` when you do.
- Worldgen output is pinned by SHA-256 characterization tests in `lib/world/generation.test.ts`; they fail on any byte-level change. See [testing.md](testing.md) for the re-baseline policy. - Durable gear restores at a maximum count of one per slot. The v1→v2 migration
  splits legacy stacked gear into separate slots until inventory capacity is
  exhausted; current malformed stacks are clamped to one.
- Note save-format/worldgen impact in PRs.

1	# Changelog
2	
3	All notable changes to this project are documented in this file.
4	
5	## [Unreleased]
6	
7	## [0.8.0] - 2026-06-14
8	
9	### Changed
10	
11	- Starting play now requires a double-click to acquire pointer lock, preventing an accidental single click from immediately capturing the mouse. No save-format or worldgen impact.
12	- Emergency unstuck now requires **`Shift` + `U`** instead of a bare `U`, so a stray keypress can no longer teleport the player mid-play. The automatic unstuck safeguard (which fires when wedged in terrain or falling below the world) is unchanged. No save-format or worldgen impact.
13	- Placed glass now renders as a clear, low-reflection transparent layer. Internal faces between adjacent glass blocks are culled, while neighboring opaque block faces remain visible through it. No save-format or worldgen impact.
14	
15	### Added
16	
17	- **Caves & lighting**: caves are no longer lit like the surface — a real per-voxel light system makes underground dark, with torches, deep-cave lava, and drowning as new hazards. All procedural, **zero new assets**
18	  - **Per-voxel light propagation** (`lib/world/lighting.ts`): each voxel carries packed sky + block light (0–15 each), baked from the blocks at load (top-down sunlight column pass + flood) and patched locally on every edit with a Minecraft-style remove/refill flood. It is a **derived cache, never serialized** (a pure function of `world.blocks`). The mesher emits a per-vertex `aLight` attribute and the world material's shader gates scene-lit terrain by sky exposure (caves go dark) while adding block light back as a glow — so **day/night needs no re-mesh** (the scene sun/hemisphere already scale with daylight)
19	  - **Torches**: craft four from one wood and place them to light the dark; a torch is a solid block emitting block light 14, so its warm glow floods the surrounding air and survives the night
20	  - **Lava**: pools in the deepest caves (carved air at or below `lavaLevel`), glowing and emitting max block light. Touching it burns **immediately** for 3 hearts every half-second with no grace period, bypassing armor, and keeps burning briefly after you escape. Worldgen-only — no item, can't be mined
21	  - **Drowning**: a bubble meter (above the hunger bar) drains over ~15 s while your head is underwater, then deals 1 heart/second until you surface; it refills quickly. Distinct from the existing 60 s body-immersion damage — wading chest-deep never drowns you
22	  - **Worldgen re-baseline**: the deep-cave lava changes the deterministic terrain baseline, so the worldgen/meshing hashes were re-rolled and **`SAVE_KEY` bumped `minecraft_save_v6` → `minecraft_save_v7`** — existing worlds reset. The save _schema_ is unchanged (lighting is derived, lava is worldgen; neither is persisted), so the payload version stays 5. `placeLava` runs after `placeOres` and before `placeDungeons`, keeping the surface byte-identical (structural probes stay green)
23	- **Spears and non-stackable gear**: seven craftable spear tiers (wood, stone,
24	  sliver, ruby, sapphire, gold, diamond) have 7-block left-click melee reach and
25	  can be thrown with right-click/`E`. Throws use procedural projectile meshes,
26	  gravity, swept mob collision, terrain collision, a cooldown, tiered damage,
27	  and one durability per throw. Missed throws remain visibly embedded in terrain
28	  for two seconds, and the faster, flatter trajectory travels farther. All
29	  durable armor, tools, knives, swords, and spears now occupy one slot across
30	  drops, crafting, saves, and chests; legacy stacked durable gear is split
31	  during migration. No save-format or worldgen impact.
32	- **Wood doors**: craft one from 6 planks and place it on a solid floor to create a thin, two-block-tall panel. Right-click either half to open or close the whole door; open doors rotate onto their hinge edge, while closed doors block players and mobs. Door facing, open state, and both halves persist through the existing block-diff save, and breaking either half removes the whole door and returns one item. Only the player interaction path toggles doors; mobs stop at closed doors and cannot operate them. No save-format or worldgen impact.
33	- **Water building and exposure damage**: block placement may now replace water cells, so underwater structures can be built against submerged terrain. Remaining continuously immersed for more than 60 seconds starts dealing 3 HP (1.5 hearts) of armor-bypassing damage every second; leaving water fully resets both timers. Exposure is session-only and is not serialized. No save-format or worldgen impact.
34	- **Endgame & ranged combat**: the game gains its first ranged weapon, ranged enemies, and a true win condition — all on one new transient projectile system, with **no save-format or worldgen change** and **zero new assets** (procedural pixel sprites + synthesized sounds)
35	  - **Projectile system** (`lib/game/engine/projectiles.ts`, `engine/systems/projectileAI.ts`): arrows are session-only entities (like mobs, never serialized) that integrate under gravity and despawn on a hit, a TTL, or leaving the world. Block collision reuses the world DDA (`voxelRaycast`), which already sweeps the whole segment, so even a very fast arrow can't tunnel a 1-block wall; the entity test is substepped too so a fast arrow can't skip a thin mob between frames. A `fromPlayer` flag is the hit filter — player arrows hit mobs (with knockback), mob arrows hit the player (armor-mitigated) — so a mob's arrow can never hit the firer or another mob. `tickProjectiles` runs right after `tickMobs` in both the live and dead step branches
36	  - **Bow & arrows**: craft a **bow** (3 wood + 3 string) and **arrows** (1 stone + 1 wood + 1 feather → 4). Holding a bow makes the attack input fire instead of melee — **instant click-to-fire** (no draw-charge; holding left-click already means mine) at a fixed damage on a short cooldown, spending one arrow and a point of bow durability per shot. The swing animation still plays
37	  - **Ranged skeletons**: a `ranged` flag on the mob template makes skeletons **kite** — backing off inside a standoff band, holding in the middle, approaching only when far — and loose arrows from across their detect range (leading a moving target) instead of meleeing. Finally distinct from zombies, which stay melee
38	  - **Endgame boss & victory**: craft a **Cursed Totem** (1 diamond ore + 2 bone + 2 gold ore — the diamond grind's first real goal) and right-click to summon a towering boss nearby (refused if one already walks). It bears down on the player, bites for heavy damage up close, looses a 3-arrow spread at range, periodically conjures minions (capped, under the global hostile cap), and is immune to the daylight burn. Defeating it drops a **Dragon Heart** that crafts the best-in-game **Dragon Sword** (60 attack), fires a one-shot **victory screen**, and shows a top-center **boss health bar** while it lives
39	  - New `"boss"` `MobKind` touches all five exhaustive `Record<MobKind>` tables (templates, drops, ambience intervals, ambient + attack sounds). New events (`arrowHit`, `bowFired`, `bossSummoned`, `bossDefeated`, `summonFailed`) drive procedural impact sparks, a conjuring column, a victory burst, and synthesized bow-twang / arrow-tick / boss-roar / victory-fanfare sounds. In-flight arrows render as a pooled extruded-sprite mesh (one shared geometry/material) oriented along their velocity
40	  - **No version bump**: the boss, its minions, projectiles, and the victory flag are all transient; the new items (bow, arrow, Cursed Totem, Dragon Heart, Dragon Sword) are additive, saved by string id. New tunables live in the `config.ts` "Ranged combat & endgame" group

# Save format & compatibility

## Schema

`SaveData` (version 5) in `lib/game/types.ts`:

- world `seed`
- a block **diff** list — `changes: [blockIndex, blockId][]`; edits that revert to the generated baseline are pruned (player-placed crops, beds, furnaces, chests, and both halves/states of doors ride this list — they are ordinary block edits)
- inventory slots with durability (36 slots; the first 9 are the hotbar)
- equipped armor
- selected hotbar slot (0–8)
- player position
- `dayClock`, `hearts`, `hunger` (all optional) — time of day and player stats, so sleeping through the night and a hurt/hungry player survive a reload
- `spawnPoint` (optional, `{x,y,z}` or null) — the bed respawn point; respawn falls back to a random land point when it is null or the block there is no longer a bed
- `blockEntities` (optional) — chest contents as `{ index, slots }[]`, keyed by the block's voxel index (the same index space as `changes`). Only **non-empty** chests are stored; an empty one carries no data and is recreated empty when opened. On load each entry is kept only if that index still holds a Chest block. This is the first per-block metadata in the format — `lib/game/save.ts` (`serializeContainers` / `readContainers`) handles it
- `lootedChests` (optional) — voxel indices of dungeon loot chests the player has already opened or broken. Dungeon chests are placed by worldgen, so their contents are **not** in `changes`/`blockEntities` until accessed; the engine fills them lazily on first access (loot seeded from `world.seed ^ index`) and records the index here. Because an emptied chest drops out of `blockEntities`, this set — not the chest's emptiness — is what prevents a re-roll on reload. The session-only set of _which_ indices are dungeon chests/spawners is not stored; it is re-derived from the seed each load via `collectDungeonSites` (`lib/world/generation.ts`). Handled by `serializeLootedChests` / `readLootedChests` in `lib/game/save.ts`

Stored in localStorage under `SAVE_KEY` (`minecraft_save_v7`, defined in `lib/game/config.ts`). Read/write and restore validation live in `lib/game/save.ts` (the `Storage` is injectable for tests); `GameEngine.serialize()` produces the save from live state, and `lib/game/engine/blockChanges.ts` maintains the block diff.

Audio volume preferences live under a **separate** key (`minecraft_audio_v1`, `lib/game/audio/settings.ts`) and are not part of the world save or its versioning.

**Per-voxel light is never serialized.** It is a derived cache (`world.light`), recomputed from the blocks at load by `computeFullLight` and patched locally on every edit (`lib/world/lighting.ts`); the bake reads only `world.blocks`, so the save needs no lighting field.

Continuous-water exposure, lava burn, and the oxygen/drowning meter all live only
in transient `GameTimers`/state. Saving, reloading, or respawning resets them
(breath restores to full).

### Version history

- **v5** (unchanged for caves & lighting) — the lighting system adds no persisted state (light is a derived cache, recomputed at load), and lava is worldgen, not a saved field. So the save _schema_ stays at version 5. But the deep-cave lava changes the deterministic terrain baseline, so **`SAVE_KEY` is bumped `minecraft_save_v6` → `minecraft_save_v7`**: old block-diffs were computed against the lava-free world and must never be applied to the new one. Pre-lava saves are discarded in practice. Torches are additive items/blocks, persisted by string id / in the block diff like any other placed block.
- **v5** (unchanged for ranged combat & the endgame boss) — bows, arrows, the Cursed Totem, the Dragon Heart, and the Dragon Sword are **additive items**, persisted by string id in the existing inventory/container slots, so no schema change was needed. **Arrows in flight, the boss, its minions, and the `victory` flag are all transient** (never serialized — like mobs), and there is no worldgen change (the boss is summoned, not generated), so neither the `version` nor `SAVE_KEY` moved.
- **v5** — adds optional `lootedChests` (opened/broken dungeon loot chests). `migrateSaveV4toV5` is a pure version bump (absent → no dungeon chests yet looted). Unlike v3/v4, **`SAVE_KEY` is bumped to `minecraft_save_v6`** here — not because of the save _shape_ (the field is additive) but because the dungeon worldgen changed the deterministic terrain baseline, so old block-diffs would index against the wrong world. Pre-dungeon saves are therefore discarded in practice; the migration keeps the version chain complete regardless. `readSave` chains v1 → v2 → v3 → v4 → v5.
- **v4** — adds optional `blockEntities` (chest contents). `migrateSaveV3toV4` is a pure version bump (absent → restores as no containers), so **`SAVE_KEY` was unchanged** at the time (player-placed chests only; worldgen and the index formula were untouched) and v1/v2/v3 saves load fine.
- **v3** — adds optional `dayClock`, `hearts`, `hunger`, and `spawnPoint`. `migrateSaveV2toV3` is a pure version bump (the new fields stay absent and restore as engine defaults), so **`SAVE_KEY` is unchanged** and v1/v2 saves load fine.
- **v2** — same fields as v1, reinterpreted for the 36-slot inventory and 9-slot hotbar.
- **v1** — 40 slots, 10-slot hotbar. Still accepted: `readSave` runs `migrateSaveV1toV2`, which packs non-empty slots in order, merges stackable items into earlier stacks, clamps `selectedSlot` to 0–8, and drops items that overflow the smaller inventory.
- Unknown future versions are rejected (treated as no save).

Every 15s via `setInterval`, plus on `beforeunload`.

  splits legacy stacked gear into separate slots until inventory capacity is
  exhausted; current malformed stacks are clamped to one.
- Note save-format/worldgen impact in PRs.

## Profiles & worlds

Saves are organized two levels deep — a **profile** owns a list of **worlds**, and each world holds one `SaveData` blob — across three localStorage keys. All three are versioned `{ version: 1, ... }` envelopes and their readers are **total** (malformed entries are dropped, never thrown):

- **`minecraft_profiles_v1`** (`lib/game/profiles.ts`) — the profile list plus `activeProfileId`. A profile is `{ id, name, skinId, createdAt }`: player identity only (name + skin). The skin moved here from the old global `minecraft_skin_v1` key; a dangling `activeProfileId` is repaired on read.
- **`minecraft_worlds_v1`** (`lib/game/worlds.ts`) — the world index. Each `WorldMeta` is `{ id, profileId, name, seed, worldgenVersion, createdAt, lastPlayedAt }`; `profileId` is the 1:N owner link and `lastPlayedAt` drives the most-recent-first ordering. The `seed` is resolved once at creation (blank → random, numeric text → clamped int, other text → stable FNV hash via `resolveSeed`) and is the source of truth for regeneration.
- **`minecraft_world_save_<worldId>`** — one `SaveData` blob per world (the schema above), read/written through `readSave`/`writeSave`.

`worldgenVersion` records the `WORLDGEN_VERSION` (`lib/game/config.ts`, currently 7) the world was generated under. This **replaces the old whole-store `SAVE_KEY` bump**: when the worldgen baseline changes, bump `WORLDGEN_VERSION`, and a world whose recorded version differs has its stale block-diffs discarded and reboots from its stored seed — per-world, with no key rename and without touching unaffected worlds.

The game shell (`components/GameShell.tsx`) drives a profile-select → world-select → play state machine and remembers the tab's active world in `sessionStorage` so a reload resumes it (a fresh tab cold-starts at profile-select). Deleting a profile cascades its worlds and their save blobs (`deleteWorldsForProfile`).

### Legacy migration

`migrateLegacySave` (`lib/game/legacyMigration.ts`) runs once on first boot, gated on the **absence** of `minecraft_profiles_v1` (its presence is the already-migrated flag, which survives a rollback that re-creates the legacy key). It creates a default "Player" profile carrying the old global skin, and — if a legacy `minecraft_save_v7` exists — **copies** it into one "My World" blob, then removes the legacy key. The copy precedes the delete so a mid-migration failure can never lose the original.

# Save format & compatibility

## Schema

`SaveData` (version 5) in `lib/game/types.ts`:

- world `seed`
- a block **diff** list — `changes: [blockIndex, blockId][]`; edits that revert to the generated baseline are pruned (player-placed crops, beds, furnaces, chests, and both halves/states of doors ride this list — they are ordinary block edits)
- inventory slots with durability (36 slots; the first 9 are the hotbar)
- equipped armor
- selected hotbar slot (0–8)
- player position
- `dayClock`, `hearts`, `hunger` (all optional) — time of day and player stats, so sleeping through the night and a hurt/hungry player survive a reload
- `spawnPoint` (optional, `{x,y,z}` or null) — the bed respawn point; respawn falls back to a random land point when it is null or the block there is no longer a bed
- `blockEntities` (optional) — chest contents as `{ index, slots }[]`, keyed by the block's voxel index (the same index space as `changes`). Only **non-empty** chests are stored; an empty one carries no data and is recreated empty when opened. On load each entry is kept only if that index still holds a Chest block. This is the first per-block metadata in the format — `lib/game/save.ts` (`serializeContainers` / `readContainers`) handles it
- `lootedChests` (optional) — voxel indices of dungeon loot chests the player has already opened or broken. Dungeon chests are placed by worldgen, so their contents are **not** in `changes`/`blockEntities` until accessed; the engine fills them lazily on first access (loot seeded from `world.seed ^ index`) and records the index here. Because an emptied chest drops out of `blockEntities`, this set — not the chest's emptiness — is what prevents a re-roll on reload. The session-only set of _which_ indices are dungeon chests/spawners is not stored; it is re-derived from the seed each load via `collectDungeonSites` (`lib/world/generation.ts`). Handled by `serializeLootedChests` / `readLootedChests` in `lib/game/save.ts`

Each world's `SaveData` is stored in its own localStorage key, `minecraft_world_save_<worldId>` (`worldSaveKey` in `lib/game/worlds.ts`). Read/write and restore validation live in `lib/game/save.ts` — `readSave`/`writeSave` take the key as a parameter and the `Storage` is injectable for tests; `GameEngine.serialize()` produces the save from live state, and `lib/game/engine/blockChanges.ts` maintains the block diff. (The legacy single-world key `SAVE_KEY` = `minecraft_save_v7` is now read only once, by the migration described under [Profiles & worlds](#profiles--worlds).)

Audio volume preferences live under a **separate**, global key (`minecraft_audio_v1`, `lib/game/audio/settings.ts`), shared across all profiles and not part of any world save or its versioning.

**Per-voxel light is never serialized.** It is a derived cache (`world.light`), recomputed from the blocks at load by `computeFullLight` and patched locally on every edit (`lib/world/lighting.ts`); the bake reads only `world.blocks`, so the save needs no lighting field.

Continuous-water exposure, lava burn, and the oxygen/drowning meter all live only
in transient `GameTimers`/state. Saving, reloading, or respawning resets them
(breath restores to full).

### Version history

- **v5** (unchanged for caves & lighting) — the lighting system adds no persisted state (light is a derived cache, recomputed at load), and lava is worldgen, not a saved field. So the save _schema_ stays at version 5. But the deep-cave lava changes the deterministic terrain baseline, so **`SAVE_KEY` is bumped `minecraft_save_v6` → `minecraft_save_v7`**: old block-diffs were computed against the lava-free world and must never be applied to the new one. Pre-lava saves are discarded in practice. Torches are additive items/blocks, persisted by string id / in the block diff like any other placed block.
- **v5** (unchanged for ranged combat & the endgame boss) — bows, arrows, the Cursed Totem, the Dragon Heart, and the Dragon Sword are **additive items**, persisted by string id in the existing inventory/container slots, so no schema change was needed. **Arrows in flight, the boss, its minions, and the `victory` flag are all transient** (never serialized — like mobs), and there is no worldgen change (the boss is summoned, not generated), so neither the `version` nor `SAVE_KEY` moved.
- **v5** — adds optional `lootedChests` (opened/broken dungeon loot chests). `migrateSaveV4toV5` is a pure version bump (absent → no dungeon chests yet looted). Unlike v3/v4, **`SAVE_KEY` is bumped to `minecraft_save_v6`** here — not because of the save _shape_ (the field is additive) but because the dungeon worldgen changed the deterministic terrain baseline, so old block-diffs would index against the wrong world. Pre-dungeon saves are therefore discarded in practice; the migration keeps the version chain complete regardless. `readSave` chains v1 → v2 → v3 → v4 → v5.
- **v4** — adds optional `blockEntities` (chest contents). `migrateSaveV3toV4` is a pure version bump (absent → restores as no containers), so **`SAVE_KEY` was unchanged** at the time (player-placed chests only; worldgen and the index formula were untouched) and v1/v2/v3 saves load fine.
- **v3** — adds optional `dayClock`, `hearts`, `hunger`, and `spawnPoint`. `migrateSaveV2toV3` is a pure version bump (the new fields stay absent and restore as engine defaults), so **`SAVE_KEY` is unchanged** and v1/v2 saves load fine.
- **v2** — same fields as v1, reinterpreted for the 36-slot inventory and 9-slot hotbar.
- **v1** — 40 slots, 10-slot hotbar. Still accepted: `readSave` runs `migrateSaveV1toV2`, which packs non-empty slots in order, merges stackable items into earlier stacks, clamps `selectedSlot` to 0–8, and drops items that overflow the smaller inventory.
- Unknown future versions are rejected (treated as no save).

## Profiles & worlds

Saves are organized two levels deep — a **profile** owns a list of **worlds**, and each world holds one `SaveData` blob — across three localStorage keys. All three are versioned `{ version: 1, ... }` envelopes and their readers are **total** (malformed entries are dropped, never thrown):

- **`minecraft_profiles_v1`** (`lib/game/profiles.ts`) — the profile list plus `activeProfileId`. A profile is `{ id, name, skinId, createdAt }`: player identity only (name + skin). The skin moved here from the old global `minecraft_skin_v1` key; a dangling `activeProfileId` is repaired on read.
- **`minecraft_worlds_v1`** (`lib/game/worlds.ts`) — the world index. Each `WorldMeta` is `{ id, profileId, name, seed, worldgenVersion, createdAt, lastPlayedAt }`; `profileId` is the 1:N owner link and `lastPlayedAt` drives the most-recent-first ordering. The `seed` is resolved once at creation (blank → random, numeric text → clamped int, other text → stable FNV hash via `resolveSeed`) and is the source of truth for regeneration.
- **`minecraft_world_save_<worldId>`** — one `SaveData` blob per world (the schema above), read/written through `readSave`/`writeSave`.

`worldgenVersion` records the `WORLDGEN_VERSION` (`lib/game/config.ts`, currently 7) the world was generated under. This **replaces the old whole-store `SAVE_KEY` bump**: when the worldgen baseline changes, bump `WORLDGEN_VERSION`, and a world whose recorded version differs has its stale block-diffs discarded and reboots from its stored seed — per-world, with no key rename and without touching unaffected worlds.

The game shell (`components/GameShell.tsx`) drives a profile-select → world-select → play state machine and remembers the tab's active world in `sessionStorage` so a reload resumes it (a fresh tab cold-starts at profile-select). Deleting a profile cascades its worlds and their save blobs (`deleteWorldsForProfile`).

### Legacy migration

`migrateLegacySave` (`lib/game/legacyMigration.ts`) runs once on first boot, gated on the **absence** of `minecraft_profiles_v1` (its presence is the already-migrated flag, which survives a rollback that re-creates the legacy key). It creates a default "Player" profile carrying the old global skin, and — if a legacy `minecraft_save_v7` exists — **copies** it into one "My World" blob, then removes the legacy key. The copy precedes the delete so a mid-migration failure can never lose the original.

## Autosave

Every 15s via `setInterval`, plus on `beforeunload`.

- Saves store **diffs against generated terrain**, so changing world generation or the voxel index formula (`x + z*sizeX + y*sizeX*sizeZ`) silently corrupts existing saves — bump `SAVE_KEY` when you do.

- Changing the save shape requires bumping the `version` field and handling (or discarding) old data. Round-trip tests live in `lib/game/save.test.ts` and `lib/game/engine/GameEngine.test.ts`.
- Durable gear restores at a maximum count of one per slot. The v1→v2 migration
  splits legacy stacked gear into separate slots until inventory capacity is
  exhausted; current malformed stacks are clamped to one.
- Note save-format/worldgen impact in PRs.

## [Unreleased]

### Added

- **Multiple worlds & player profiles**: the game now opens to a menu instead of dropping straight into one fixed world. A **profile** (name + skin) owns a list of named **worlds**, like user accounts on a shared console — pick a profile, then pick or create a world to play. All client-side in localStorage; **zero new assets** (the menus reuse the existing Minecraft-style chrome and generated skin portraits)
  - **Two-level save hierarchy** (`lib/game/profiles.ts`, `lib/game/worlds.ts`): a versioned `minecraft_profiles_v1` manifest (`{ id, name, skinId, createdAt }` + `activeProfileId`) and a `minecraft_worlds_v1` index (`{ id, profileId, name, seed, worldgenVersion, createdAt, lastPlayedAt }`), with each world's `SaveData` in its own `minecraft_world_save_<id>` key. Readers are total — malformed entries are dropped and a dangling active profile is repaired. New-world seeds are resolved once at creation (blank → random, numeric → clamped, other text → stable FNV hash). The skin moved off the old global `minecraft_skin_v1` key onto the profile; **audio settings stay global**
  - **Menu shell** (`components/GameShell.tsx`, `components/menu/*`): a profile-select → world-select → play state machine with create / rename / delete on both levels (deleting a profile cascades its worlds and their save blobs). Switching worlds, Load, or Reset remounts the game subtree via a React `key`, so the engine/renderer are disposed and re-created **without a page reload**. The tab remembers its active world in `sessionStorage`, so a reload resumes straight back into play while a fresh tab cold-starts at the menu. The pause menu gains **Save & Quit to Worlds**
  - **Per-world worldgen versioning**: each world records the `WORLDGEN_VERSION` it was generated under (`lib/game/config.ts`). A future worldgen change bumps that constant and discards only the affected worlds' stale block-diffs (rebooting them from their seed) — replacing the old whole-store `SAVE_KEY` rename, which reset every world. The save _schema_ is unchanged (still version 5)

## [Unreleased]

### Added

- **Multiple worlds & player profiles**: the game now opens to a menu instead of dropping straight into one fixed world. A **profile** (name + skin) owns a list of named **worlds**, like user accounts on a shared console — pick a profile, then pick or create a world to play. All client-side in localStorage; **zero new assets** (the menus reuse the existing Minecraft-style chrome and generated skin portraits)
  - **Two-level save hierarchy** (`lib/game/profiles.ts`, `lib/game/worlds.ts`): a versioned `minecraft_profiles_v1` manifest (`{ id, name, skinId, createdAt }` + `activeProfileId`) and a `minecraft_worlds_v1` index (`{ id, profileId, name, seed, worldgenVersion, createdAt, lastPlayedAt }`), with each world's `SaveData` in its own `minecraft_world_save_<id>` key. Readers are total — malformed entries are dropped and a dangling active profile is repaired. New-world seeds are resolved once at creation (blank → random, numeric → clamped, other text → stable FNV hash). The skin moved off the old global `minecraft_skin_v1` key onto the profile; **audio settings stay global**
  - **Menu shell** (`components/GameShell.tsx`, `components/menu/*`): a profile-select → world-select → play state machine with create / rename / delete on both levels (deleting a profile cascades its worlds and their save blobs). The tab remembers its active world in `sessionStorage`, so a reload resumes straight back into play while a fresh tab cold-starts at the menu. The pause menu gains **Save & Quit to Worlds**
  - **Per-world worldgen versioning**: each world records the `WORLDGEN_VERSION` it was generated under (`lib/game/config.ts`).
