# Player Manual

A complete guide to playing Monecraft — a single-player, browser-based voxel
sandbox. Mine, build, craft, farm, fight off the night, and survive.

This page is the prose guide; for the exact numbers (every recipe, block, mob, and
item stat) see the [reference tables](reference.md). Just want the keys? They're in
the [README](../README.md#controls).

> Everything you see and hear is generated from code at runtime — there are no
> image or audio files anywhere in the game.

## Getting started: your first day

You spawn at dawn on solid ground with a small starter kit: stacks of grass, dirt,
stone, wood, planks, cobble, and sand, plus a **wood pickaxe** and a **knife**.

The day-night cycle is short — **four minutes per full day** — so the first night
comes fast. A good opening:

1. **Look around.** Double-click the game to lock the mouse (the starting gesture
   doesn't mine). Move with `W A S D`, look with the mouse.
2. **Gear up from your kit.** Open the inventory with **`I`**. You already have
   cobble and wood, so craft a **stone pickaxe** (2 cobble + 1 wood) and a **stone
   sword** (2 cobble + 1 wood) — both upgrades over your starting wood pickaxe and
   knife.
3. **Mine and gather.** Hold **left-click** to break trees, stone, and dirt for
   more materials; craft **2 wood → 4 planks** whenever you need them.
4. **Shelter before dark.** Wall yourself in with blocks (**right-click** or `E`
   to place the selected hotbar item), or craft a **bed** and skip the night
   entirely. Hostile mobs spawn once it gets dark, so don't be caught in the open.

From there it's a sandbox: dig for ores, build, farm, breed animals, and gear up.

## Controls

| Key / input        | Action                                                              |
| ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `W` `A` `S` `D`    | Move (walk / strafe)                                                |
| `Space`            | Jump                                                                |

## Worlds & profiles

The game opens to a menu rather than dropping you straight into a world:

1. **Pick a profile.** A profile is a player — a name and an appearance (skin). On a
   shared browser everyone can have their own. Create one with **New Profile**, choose
   a skin, and you're in; rename or delete profiles from the same screen.
2. **Pick a world.** Each profile keeps its **own** list of worlds. **New World** lets
   you name it and, optionally, enter a **seed** — type a number or a word to get the
   same world every time, or leave it blank for a random one. Worlds you've played show
   most-recent first; rename or delete them here too.
3. **Play.** Choosing a world drops you in. From the pause menu (**Esc**), **Save &
   Quit to Worlds** takes you back to the list, and reloading the page resumes the
   world you were in.

Everything is saved in your browser (localStorage). Deleting a world removes its save;
deleting a profile removes all of its worlds.

docs/testing.md:65:The **deep-cave lava worldgen** is the most recent legitimate re-baseline (case 1): the four worldgen digests and the in-region meshing snapshot were re-rolled and `SAVE_KEY` bumped v6 → v7. As with dungeons the structural probes (surface heights/biomes/snow/water) were left unchanged on purpose — `placeLava` runs after `placeOres` so it can't shift the ore→tree RNG stream, and the lava sits at or below `lavaLevel`, so the surface is byte-identical. A probe asserts lava is present and never rises above `lavaLevel`. Note the per-voxel **lighting** change re-rolled nothing: light is a derived runtime cache, never part of the generated bytes, and the meshing snapshot hashes only vertex positions — the new `aLight` attribute leaves them untouched.
docs/testing.md:67:The **0.7.0 dungeon worldgen** was the prior re-baseline (case 1): the four worldgen digests and the in-region meshing snapshot were re-rolled and `SAVE_KEY` bumped v5 → v6. The structural probes were left unchanged — dungeons are wholly underground, so the surface bytes are identical.
docs/save-format.md:18:Each world's `SaveData` is stored in its own localStorage key, `minecraft_world_save_<worldId>` (`worldSaveKey` in `lib/game/worlds.ts`). Read/write and restore validation live in `lib/game/save.ts` — `readSave`/`writeSave` take the key as a parameter and the `Storage` is injectable for tests; `GameEngine.serialize()` produces the save from live state, and `lib/game/engine/blockChanges.ts` maintains the block diff. (The legacy single-world key `SAVE_KEY` = `minecraft_save_v7` is now read only once, by the migration described under [Profiles & worlds](#profiles--worlds).)
docs/save-format.md:30:- **v5** (unchanged for caves & lighting) — the lighting system adds no persisted state (light is a derived cache, recomputed at load), and lava is worldgen, not a saved field. So the save _schema_ stays at version 5. But the deep-cave lava changes the deterministic terrain baseline, so **`SAVE_KEY` is bumped `minecraft_save_v6` → `minecraft_save_v7`**: old block-diffs were computed against the lava-free world and must never be applied to the new one. Pre-lava saves are discarded in practice. Torches are additive items/blocks, persisted by string id / in the block diff like any other placed block.
docs/save-format.md:31:- **v5** (unchanged for ranged combat & the endgame boss) — bows, arrows, the Cursed Totem, the Dragon Heart, and the Dragon Sword are **additive items**, persisted by string id in the existing inventory/container slots, so no schema change was needed. **Arrows in flight, the boss, its minions, and the `victory` flag are all transient** (never serialized — like mobs), and there is no worldgen change (the boss is summoned, not generated), so neither the `version` nor `SAVE_KEY` moved.
docs/save-format.md:32:- **v5** — adds optional `lootedChests` (opened/broken dungeon loot chests). `migrateSaveV4toV5` is a pure version bump (absent → no dungeon chests yet looted). Unlike v3/v4, **`SAVE_KEY` is bumped to `minecraft_save_v6`** here — not because of the save _shape_ (the field is additive) but because the dungeon worldgen changed the deterministic terrain baseline, so old block-diffs would index against the wrong world. Pre-dungeon saves are therefore discarded in practice; the migration keeps the version chain complete regardless. `readSave` chains v1 → v2 → v3 → v4 → v5.
docs/save-format.md:33:- **v4** — adds optional `blockEntities` (chest contents). `migrateSaveV3toV4` is a pure version bump (absent → restores as no containers), so **`SAVE_KEY` was unchanged** at the time (player-placed chests only; worldgen and the index formula were untouched) and v1/v2/v3 saves load fine.
docs/save-format.md:34:- **v3** — adds optional `dayClock`, `hearts`, `hunger`, and `spawnPoint`. `migrateSaveV2toV3` is a pure version bump (the new fields stay absent and restore as engine defaults), so **`SAVE_KEY` is unchanged** and v1/v2 saves load fine.
docs/save-format.md:43:- **`minecraft_profiles_v1`** (`lib/game/profiles.ts`) — the profile list plus `activeProfileId`. A profile is `{ id, name, skinId, createdAt }`: player identity only (name + skin). The skin moved here from the old global `minecraft_skin_v1` key; a dangling `activeProfileId` is repaired on read.
docs/save-format.md:47:`worldgenVersion` records the `WORLDGEN_VERSION` (`lib/game/config.ts`, currently 7) the world was generated under. This **replaces the old whole-store `SAVE_KEY` bump**: when the worldgen baseline changes, bump `WORLDGEN_VERSION`, and a world whose recorded version differs has its stale block-diffs discarded and reboots from its stored seed — per-world, with no key rename and without touching unaffected worlds.
docs/save-format.md:53:`migrateLegacySave` (`lib/game/legacyMigration.ts`) runs once on first boot, gated on the **absence** of `minecraft_profiles_v1` (its presence is the already-migrated flag, which survives a rollback that re-creates the legacy key). It creates a default "Player" profile carrying the old global skin, and — if a legacy `minecraft_save_v7` exists — **copies** it into one "My World" blob, then removes the legacy key. The copy precedes the delete so a mid-migration failure can never lose the original.

## Persistence & rendering

`AUTOSAVE_INTERVAL_MS`, `SAVE_KEY`, `STUCK_RESET_SECONDS`, `RENDER_RADIUS`,
`RENDER_GRID`, `THIRD_PERSON_DISTANCE`, `THIRD_PERSON_MARGIN`.

`RENDER_RADIUS` is the biggest **performance** lever: the renderer meshes one region
of this radius around the player, so larger values draw more terrain at higher cost;
`RENDER_GRID` is how far the player moves before that mesh rebuilds (smaller = more
frequent rebuilds, fresher view). `STUCK_RESET_SECONDS` is how long an overlap is
tolerated before the auto-unstuck teleport fires.

84	## A worldgen structure (houses, dungeons, …)
85	
86	- Structures are placed in `lib/world/generation.ts` at the end of the `generateWorld` pipeline. Mirror `placeHouse`/`placeDungeons`: loop a `GEN.<thing>Count`, sample positions, validate, and write blocks with `world.set`. Append your pass **last** so later passes don't overwrite it, and add the count to the frozen `GEN` object.
87	- **Any block write changes the deterministic output**, so this breaks the worldgen hash. Re-baseline the `generation.test.ts` digests and bump `SAVE_KEY` per the [testing.md](testing.md) policy; add a structural probe test (count your blocks, assert they generate) that survives the re-baseline.
88	- If the structure needs its positions known at runtime (dungeons re-derive chest/spawner indices on load), expose a **derive pass** like `collectDungeonSites`: factor placement into a shared routine that either writes blocks or records indices, drawing from a **dedicated PRNG seeded only from `world.seed`** (not the shared gen stream) with a fixed number of draws per structure, and validate against **seed-pure** terrain (`terrainTopY`, `getBiome`) — never `highestSolidY`, which a cave or player edit can shift out from under the derive pass.

## A worldgen structure (houses, dungeons, …)

- Structures are placed in `lib/world/generation.ts` at the end of the `generateWorld` pipeline. All 13 e2e tests pass. The feature is complete and the full verify gate is green. Here's the summary.

## Multiple Worlds & Player Profiles — done

Built on branch `feat/worlds-and-profiles` as the model you chose: **profiles own worlds** (name + skin per profile, audio stays global), shipped as one feature in six focused commits.

```
7b60826 feat(save): add versioned profile and world manifests
24a9e63 feat(save): migrate the legacy single save into a default profile + world
3fea321 refactor(game): drive the game by a selected world and profile
92342a6 feat(menu): add profile and world selection menus
2f6e3f3 test(e2e): cover the menu flow and in-app world switching
278a5b4 docs: document profiles, worlds, and the per-world save model
```

**What it does**
- Opens to a **profile-select → world-select → play** menu (create / rename / delete on both levels, optional seed entry).
- Each profile keeps its own worlds; each world saves to its own `minecraft_world_save_<id>` key. Skin moved onto the profile; audio stays global.
- Switching worlds / Load / Reset remounts the game via a React `key` — old engine/renderer disposed, new one booted, **no page reload**. The tab remembers its world in `sessionStorage`, so a reload resumes straight back into play.
- A one-time migration folds any existing single-world save into a default "Player" profile + "My World" (copy-before-delete, idempotent).
- New per-world `WORLDGEN_VERSION` replaces the old whole-store `SAVE_KEY` bump: a future worldgen change discards only affected worlds' stale diffs.

**Verification (all green):** `lint`, `typecheck`, `format:check`, `build`, **494 unit/component tests**, **13 Playwright e2e** (10 gameplay through the menu + 3 menu/world-switch). Docs updated across save-format, architecture, testing, tuning, adding-content, manual, README, and CHANGELOG.

Nothing has been pushed — the branch is local for you to review (matching your usual flow). When you want, I can open a PR against `hutusi/main`.

One product note worth surfacing: a brand-new install auto-creates a "Player" profile, so first-run lands on profile-select with one profile rather than an empty list — I judged that smoother than an empty screen, but it's a one-line change in `GameShell`/migration if you'd prefer the empty "create your first profile" state.

message.content: is it better to let the user to choose a profile with name, skin and others? what do you think?

content.text:
Good question, and it's really two questions. Let me separate them.

## Can users already choose name + skin? Yes — except on first run

Creating a profile *already* prompts for **name + skin** (`CreateProfileForm` — text field + the 6-swatch picker). So users do choose. The one gap is the **first-run auto-create**: a brand-new player gets a pre-made "Player" profile with the default skin instead of being asked. That's the thing actually worth changing.

My recommendation: on a truly fresh install (no legacy save, no profiles), drop the player **straight into the create-profile form** so their very first interaction is "who are you / pick a look," then into their empty world list. Returning players and the migrated legacy save are untouched. It's a small, localized change (the first-run branch in migration + `GameShell`) and it makes the opening feel personal instead of handing them a generic "Player."

## Should a profile carry "others" (more than name + skin)? I'd hold the line at name + skin

Here's my honest take on why *not* to pile more on:

- **A profile's job is identity + world ownership** on a shared browser. Name labels it; skin is the visual identity. That's complete for the job.
- **Most "other" things belong elsewhere.** Difficulty / game-mode is per-*world* in Minecraft (different worlds, different rules) — not per-profile. Playtime/achievements are naturally per-world and can be aggregated later without living on the profile record. Audio you already decided stays global.
- **More fields = more persistence surface** (migration, validation, UI) for little payoff. The manifests stay lean and the readers stay simple.

If the real itch is "I want *more* customization choice," the high-value place to spend it is the **skin system itself** — e.g. a custom-color option beyond the 6 presets. That's better than profile fields because it automatically shows up in *both* the create-profile form and the in-game pause picker (they share `SKIN_PRESETS` / `skinPortraitUrl`), and it's a pure `lib/game/playerSkins.ts` extension with zero save-format churn.

So, concretely, two things I'd actually do, in order of value:

1. **First-run create-profile flow** (small, clear win) — replace the silent "Player" with a "set up your profile" step.
2. **Richer skins later** (optional) — a custom-color picker if you want more expression, built into the skin system so it benefits the whole game.

Want me to do #1 now? And if richer skins appeal, I can scope #2 separately — but I'd keep the profile record itself at name + skin.

**Model:** a profile owns its worlds (1 profile : N worlds). A profile carries identity only — **name + skin**; audio settings stay global.

## What changed

- **Two-level save hierarchy** (`lib/game/profiles.ts`, `lib/game/worlds.ts`): a versioned `minecraft_profiles_v1` manifest and a `minecraft_worlds_v1` index, with each world's `SaveData` in its own `minecraft_world_save_<id>` key (via the existing `readSave`/`writeSave`, which already took a key param). Readers are total — malformed entries dropped, dangling active-profile repaired. New-world seeds resolve once at creation (blank → random, numeric → clamped, other text → stable FNV hash).
- **Menu shell** (`components/GameShell.tsx`, `components/menu/*`): profile-select → world-select → play state machine with create / rename / delete on both levels (deleting a profile cascades its worlds and their save blobs). Switching worlds, Load, or Reset remounts the game subtree via a React `key`, so the engine/renderer are disposed and re-created **without a page reload**. The tab remembers its active world in `sessionStorage`, so a reload resumes straight back into play while a fresh tab cold-starts at the menu. The pause menu gains **Save & Quit to Worlds**.
- **Per-world worldgen versioning** (`WORLDGEN_VERSION` in `config.ts`): each world records the baseline it was generated under. A future worldgen change bumps that constant and discards only the affected worlds' stale block-diffs — replacing the old whole-store `SAVE_KEY` rename, which reset every world. The save schema is unchanged (still version 5).
- **One-time migration** (`lib/game/legacyMigration.ts`): an existing single-world save is folded into a default "Player" profile (carrying the old skin) plus one "My World"; the legacy blob is copied before the old key is removed, so a failure can't lose data. Idempotent (gated on the profiles manifest's absence).
- The player skin moved off the old global `minecraft_skin_v1` key onto the profile (`updateSkin` → `setProfileSkin`).

## Save-format / worldgen impact

- New localStorage keys: `minecraft_profiles_v1`, `minecraft_worlds_v1`, `minecraft_world_save_<id>`. The legacy `minecraft_save_v7` is read once by the migration, then removed. **Existing worlds migrate automatically** into "Player / My World" — no data loss.
- No worldgen change; `WORLDGEN_VERSION` is introduced at the current baseline (7). Save schema stays v5.

## Tests

- **Unit:** `profiles.test.ts`, `worlds.test.ts`, `legacyMigration.test.ts` (manifest CRUD, total readers, seed resolution, ordering, cascade delete, copy-then-remove migration + idempotency, audio untouched).
- **Component:** `ProfileSelect` / `WorldSelect` / `CreateWorldForm` tests; `PauseMenu` test extended for Save & Quit to Worlds.
- **E2E:** new `e2e/menu.e2e.ts` (create a world with a fixed seed and play it; quit then switch worlds with no page reload; reload resumes the tab's world; a second profile gets its own world list). The smoke fixture seeds a profile + world and enters via the menu, so the existing gameplay suite passes unchanged.

Full gate green: `lint`, `typecheck`, `format:check`, `build`, 494 unit/component tests, 13 Playwright e2e.

## Docs

Updated `save-format.md` (Profiles & worlds + migration), `architecture.md` (menu shell + key-remount lifecycle, per-profile skin), `testing.md` (new coverage rows), `tuning.md` + `adding-content.md` (`WORLDGEN_VERSION` replaces the `SAVE_KEY` bump), `README.md` + `manual.md` (player flow), and `CHANGELOG.md`.

## Open follow-up (not in this PR)

First run currently auto-creates a default "Player" profile. A nice onboarding tweak would be to instead drop a brand-new player straight into the create-profile form (name + skin). Left out pending a decision.

# Save format & compatibility

## Schema

`SaveData` (version 5) in `lib/game/types.ts`:

- world `seed`
- a block **diff** list — `changes: [blockIndex, blockId][]`; edits that revert to the generated baseline are pruned (player-placed crops, beds, furnaces, chests, and both halves/states of doors ride this list — they are ordinary block edits)
- inventory slots with durability (36 slots; the first 9 are the hotbar)
- equipped armor
- selected hotbar slot (0–8)
- player position
- `dayClock`, `hearts`, `hunger` (all optional) — time of day and player stats, so sleeping through the night and a hurt/hungry player survive a reload
- `spawnPoint` (optional, `{x,y,z}` or null) — the bed respawn point; respawn falls back to a random land point when it is null or the block there is no longer a bed
- `blockEntities` (optional) — chest contents as `{ index, slots }[]`, keyed by the block's voxel index (the same index space as `changes`). Only **non-empty** chests are stored; an empty one carries no data and is recreated empty when opened. On load each entry is kept only if that index still holds a Chest block. This is the first per-block metadata in the format — `lib/game/save.ts` (`serializeContainers` / `readContainers`) handles it
- `lootedChests` (optional) — voxel indices of dungeon loot chests the player has already opened or broken. Dungeon chests are placed by worldgen, so their contents are **not** in `changes`/`blockEntities` until accessed; the engine fills them lazily on first access (loot seeded from `world.seed ^ index`) and records the index here. Because an emptied chest drops out of `blockEntities`, this set — not the chest's emptiness — is what prevents a re-roll on reload. The session-only set of _which_ indices are dungeon chests/spawners is not stored; it is re-derived from the seed each load via `collectDungeonSites` (`lib/world/generation.ts`). Handled by `serializeLootedChests` / `readLootedChests` in `lib/game/save.ts`

Each world's `SaveData` is stored in its own localStorage key, `minecraft_world_save_<worldId>` (`worldSaveKey` in `lib/game/worlds.ts`). Read/write and restore validation live in `lib/game/save.ts` — `readSave`/`writeSave` take the key as a parameter and the `Storage` is injectable for tests; `GameEngine.serialize()` produces the save from live state, and `lib/game/engine/blockChanges.ts` maintains the block diff. (The legacy single-world key `SAVE_KEY` = `minecraft_save_v7` is now read only once, by the migration described under [Profiles & worlds](#profiles--worlds).)

Audio volume preferences live under a **separate**, global key (`minecraft_audio_v1`, `lib/game/audio/settings.ts`), shared across all profiles and not part of any world save or its versioning.

**Per-voxel light is never serialized.** It is a derived cache (`world.light`), recomputed from the blocks at load by `computeFullLight` and patched locally on every edit (`lib/world/lighting.ts`); the bake reads only `world.blocks`, so the save needs no lighting field.

Continuous-water exposure, lava burn, and the oxygen/drowning meter all live only
in transient `GameTimers`/state. Saving, reloading, or respawning resets them
(breath restores to full).

### Version history

- **v5** (unchanged for caves & lighting) — the lighting system adds no persisted state (light is a derived cache, recomputed at load), and lava is worldgen, not a saved field. So the save _schema_ stays at version 5. But the deep-cave lava changes the deterministic terrain baseline, so **`SAVE_KEY` is bumped `minecraft_save_v6` → `minecraft_save_v7`**: old block-diffs were computed against the lava-free world and must never be applied to the new one. Pre-lava saves are discarded in practice. Torches are additive items/blocks, persisted by string id / in the block diff like any other placed block.
- **v5** (unchanged for ranged combat & the endgame boss) — bows, arrows, the Cursed Totem, the Dragon Heart, and the Dragon Sword are **additive items**, persisted by string id in the existing inventory/container slots, so no schema change was needed. **Arrows in flight, the boss, its minions, and the `victory` flag are all transient** (never serialized — like mobs), and there is no worldgen change (the boss is summoned, not generated), so neither the `version` nor `SAVE_KEY` moved.
- **v5** — adds optional `lootedChests` (opened/broken dungeon loot chests). `migrateSaveV4toV5` is a pure version bump (absent → no dungeon chests yet looted). Unlike v3/v4, **`SAVE_KEY` is bumped to `minecraft_save_v6`** here — not because of the save _shape_ (the field is additive) but because the dungeon worldgen changed the deterministic terrain baseline, so old block-diffs would index against the wrong world. Pre-dungeon saves are therefore discarded in practice; the migration keeps the version chain complete regardless. `readSave` chains v1 → v2 → v3 → v4 → v5.
- **v4** — adds optional `blockEntities` (chest contents). `migrateSaveV3toV4` is a pure version bump (absent → restores as no containers), so **`SAVE_KEY` was unchanged** at the time (player-placed chests only; worldgen and the index formula were untouched) and v1/v2/v3 saves load fine.
- **v3** — adds optional `dayClock`, `hearts`, `hunger`, and `spawnPoint`. `migrateSaveV2toV3` is a pure version bump (the new fields stay absent and restore as engine defaults), so **`SAVE_KEY` is unchanged** and v1/v2 saves load fine.
- **v2** — same fields as v1, reinterpreted for the 36-slot inventory and 9-slot hotbar.
- **v1** — 40 slots, 10-slot hotbar. Still accepted: `readSave` runs `migrateSaveV1toV2`, which packs non-empty slots in order, merges stackable items into earlier stacks, clamps `selectedSlot` to 0–8, and drops items that overflow the smaller inventory.
- Unknown future versions are rejected (treated as no save).

## Profiles & worlds

Saves are organized two levels deep — a **profile** owns a list of **worlds**, and each world holds one `SaveData` blob — across three localStorage keys. All three are versioned `{ version: 1, ... }` envelopes and their readers are **total** (malformed entries are dropped, never thrown):

- **`minecraft_profiles_v1`** (`lib/game/profiles.ts`) — the profile list plus `activeProfileId`. A profile is `{ id, name, skinId, createdAt }`: player identity only (name + skin). The skin moved here from the old global `minecraft_skin_v1` key; a dangling `activeProfileId` is repaired on read.
- **`minecraft_worlds_v1`** (`lib/game/worlds.ts`) — the world index. Each `WorldMeta` is `{ id, profileId, name, seed, worldgenVersion, createdAt, lastPlayedAt }`; `profileId` is the 1:N owner link and `lastPlayedAt` drives the most-recent-first ordering. The `seed` is resolved once at creation (blank → random, numeric text → clamped int, other text → stable FNV hash via `resolveSeed`) and is the source of truth for regeneration.
- **`minecraft_world_save_<worldId>`** — one `SaveData` blob per world (the schema above), read/written through `readSave`/`writeSave`.

`worldgenVersion` records the `WORLDGEN_VERSION` (`lib/game/config.ts`, currently 7) the world was generated under. This **replaces the old whole-store `SAVE_KEY` bump**: when the worldgen baseline changes, bump `WORLDGEN_VERSION`, and a world whose recorded version differs has its stale block-diffs discarded and reboots from its stored seed — per-world, with no key rename and without touching unaffected worlds.

The game shell (`components/GameShell.tsx`) drives a profile-select → world-select → play state machine and remembers the tab's active world in `sessionStorage` so a reload resumes it (a fresh tab cold-starts at profile-select). Deleting a profile cascades its worlds and their save blobs (`deleteWorldsForProfile`).

### Legacy migration

`migrateLegacySave` (`lib/game/legacyMigration.ts`) runs once on first boot, gated on the **absence** of `minecraft_profiles_v1` (its presence is the already-migrated flag, which survives a rollback that re-creates the legacy key). It creates a default "Player" profile carrying the old global skin, and — if a legacy `minecraft_save_v7` exists — **copies** it into one "My World" blob, then removes the legacy key. The copy precedes the delete so a mid-migration failure can never lose the original.

## Autosave

Every 15s via `setInterval`, plus on `beforeunload`, all writing to the active world's `minecraft_world_save_<id>` key. "Save & Quit to Worlds" also persists synchronously before leaving, because the interval is cleared on unmount and `beforeunload` does not fire on an in-app world switch.

## Compatibility rules

- Saves store **diffs against generated terrain**, so changing world generation or the voxel index formula (`x + z*sizeX + y*sizeX*sizeZ`) silently corrupts existing saves — bump `WORLDGEN_VERSION` when you do, and each world discards its stale diffs (rebooting from its seed) on the mismatch.
- Worldgen output is pinned by SHA-256 characterization tests in `lib/world/generation.test.ts`; they fail on any byte-level change. See [testing.md](testing.md) for the re-baseline policy. Caveat: the noise functions use `Math.sin`, whose exact results are engine-defined — the tests prove refactor purity on the pinned Bun version, not cross-browser save portability.
- Changing the save shape requires bumping the `version` field and handling (or discarding) old data. Round-trip tests live in `lib/game/save.test.ts` and `lib/game/engine/GameEngine.test.ts`.
- Durable gear restores at a maximum count of one per slot. The v1→v2 migration
  splits legacy stacked gear into separate slots until inventory capacity is
  exhausted; current malformed stacks are clamped to one.
- Note save-format/worldgen impact in PRs.

# Multiple Worlds & Multiple Player Profiles

## Context

Today the game has exactly one world and one implicit player. A single localStorage
key (`minecraft_save_v7`) holds the only world; the player's appearance lives in a
separate global key (`minecraft_skin_v1`). The app boots straight into that one world —
there is no title/menu, no way to keep more than one save, and no notion of distinct
players sharing a browser.

This feature adds **multiple named worlds** and **multiple player profiles**, with the
decided model: **a profile owns its worlds** (1 profile : N worlds), like user accounts
on a shared console. Selecting a profile filters the world list. A profile carries
**name + skin only**; audio settings stay global. Shipped as **one combined feature** on
one branch.

The architecture is well-suited to this: the save layer's `readSave`/`writeSave` already
take a key parameter (always called with the one constant today), the engine is fully
headless and disposable, and the mount lifecycle already tears down everything cleanly on
unmount — so worlds can be switched at runtime via a React `key` remount, with no page

In this Minecraft-inspired voxel game (Next.js + Three.js + Bun), I'm evaluating whether to add "world presets" to the new-world creation form. Today the only choice is a seed (blank = random). I need to understand how much a seed actually changes the generated world, and whether a cheap "world type" knob exists.

Explore `lib/world/generation.ts`, `lib/world/voxelWorld.ts`, `lib/world/blocks.ts`, and any biome/noise modules. Answer concretely:

1. **World size & shape**: Is every world the same fixed size (`WORLD_SIZE_X/Y/Z`)? What are the dimensions? Is it a single finite region (so all biomes coexist in one world) or infinite/chunked?

2. **How the seed drives generation**: Trace `world.seed` into terrain height, biome selection, caves, ores, structures (houses/dungeons), trees, water/lava. Does a different seed meaningfully change the world's *character* (e.g. mountainous vs flat, mostly-forest vs mostly-desert, lots of water vs little), or does every seed produce roughly the same mix because the biome map / sea level / amplitude are fixed? Quote the key constants.

3. **The `GEN` constants object**: List the tunables in the frozen `GEN` object (terrain amplitude, sea level, biome thresholds, cave density, ore rates, structure counts, dungeon count, etc.). Which of these, if parameterized per-world, would create genuinely different "world types" (e.g. superflat = amplitude 0; amplified = high amplitude; islands = high sea level; lush = forest-biased biome thresholds)? Are biomes chosen by a noise threshold I could bias?

4. **Determinism / hash contract**: How is worldgen output pinned (the SHA-256 characterization tests in `generation.test.ts`)? If I added a `worldType`/generation-parameter branch to `generateWorld`, would the *default* path stay byte-identical (so existing hashes/worlds are unaffected), or does any branch risk shifting the RNG stream? How does `WORLDGEN_VERSION` (in `lib/game/config.ts`) gate this?

5. **What `generateWorld` receives**: Does `generateWorld(world)` read ONLY `world.seed`, or could it also read a `world.worldType`/params field? How is the `VoxelWorld` constructed (in `GameEngine`'s constructor) — what would it take to thread an extra generation parameter from the save/WorldMeta into `generateWorld`?

Report with specific file paths, line numbers, the actual constant values, and a clear verdict on: (a) how much variety pure seeds give today, and (b) which "world type" knobs would be cheap vs expensive to add, and their save-format/hash implications. Be concrete — read the real code.

content.text:
Good instinct — and exploring the worldgen turned up something that sharpens the question. Here's the honest picture:

**Every world is the same fixed 512×150×512 region with all 5 biomes baked in by fixed thresholds** (sea level always 43, mountains always present, etc.). So a different seed only reshuffles *detail* — it can't give you a "desert world" or an "island world." That means there are really two different features hiding behind "presets":

1. **Curated seeds** — a few hand-picked named seeds to click instead of typing. Cheap and zero-risk, **but** because seeds barely change a world's character here, the labels would be a bit of a fib and the payoff is small.
2. **World *types*** (like Minecraft's Default / Superflat / Amplified / Islands) — actual generation variants the player chooses. This is the version that genuinely delivers "let me pick a good world." It's more work and touches the worldgen determinism contract, but the exploration confirms it's tractable: fork `generateWorld` *before* any block write so the **Default path stays byte-identical** (existing worlds untouched), add a `worldType` field to the world record + save blob, and pin each new type with its own hash test. No forced reset of existing worlds.

My recommendation: if we do this, do **world types** — curated seeds underdeliver given how this engine generates. The cleanest first set is the ones that only touch terrain config (Superflat, Amplified, maybe Islands); biome-mix types (a lush or desert world) are more invasive because they touch biome selection, not just terrain.

Let me confirm the direction and scope before I plan it:

input.plan:
# World Types in New-World Creation

## Context

The new-world form (`components/menu/CreateWorldForm.tsx`, shipped in the worlds & profiles
PR #21) only lets the player set a name and a seed ("leave blank for random"). But the
worldgen produces **one fixed 512×150×512 region with all five biomes baked in by fixed
thresholds** (sea level always 43, mountains always present) — so a different seed only
reshuffles detail; it can't give a flat, amplified, or island world. The player can't
actually choose the *character* of their world.

This adds **world types** to creation — **Default, Superflat, Amplified, Islands** (the
terrain-config-only set; biome-biased types were explicitly excluded). Each is a real
generation variant the player picks alongside name + seed. The type is fixed at creation
(like the seed) and recorded on the world.

**Determinism is preserved.** `generateWorld` forks on the type *before any block write*;
the Default branch uses the existing `GEN` values unchanged, so its output stays
byte-identical and **existing worlds and the current hash tests are untouched** — no
`WORLDGEN_VERSION` bump. Each new type is independently deterministic and gets its own hash
baseline. (Terrain generation reads `smoothNoise2D`/`hash2D`, never the `rand` PRNG, so a
terrain-config change can't desync the default stream — it only changes that type's own
downstream output, which is what we want.)

## Design

### 1. World-type definitions (world layer — `lib/world/`)

New `lib/world/worldTypes.ts` (no `GEN` dependency, so no import cycle):

```ts
export type WorldType = "default" | "flat" | "amplified" | "islands";
export const WORLD_TYPE_IDS: readonly WorldType[] = ["default", "flat", "amplified", "islands"];
export function isWorldType(v: unknown): v is WorldType { /* membership check */ }
```

Export from the `lib/world/index.ts` barrel.

### 2. Terrain config fork (`lib/world/generation.ts`)

- `generateWorld(world)` → **`generateWorld(world, worldType: WorldType = "default")`** (optional
  param ⇒ existing `generateWorld(world)` test calls stay "default" ⇒ byte-identical).
- Add `terrainConfigFor(worldType)` returning `{ seaLevel, biomes: Record<BiomeId, {baseHeight, noiseScale}> }`.
  `"default"` returns exactly `GEN.seaLevel` / `GEN.biomes` values (byte-identical path).
- Thread the config into the **only three** functions that vary; everything else
  (`carveCaves`, `placeOres`, `placeLava`, `placeTrees`, `placeCacti`, `placeStructures`,
  `placeDungeons`) keeps reading `GEN` unchanged:
  - `generateTerrain(world, cfg)` — read `cfg.biomes[biome]` (was `GEN.biomes[biome]`, line 110); keep `GEN.snowAboveY`/`mountainStoneAboveY`/`borderWallHeight`.
  - `placeWater(world, cfg)` — `cfg.seaLevel` (was `GEN.seaLevel`, line 212).
  - `placeBeaches(world, cfg)` — `cfg.seaLevel` (lines 275, 281).
- Starting config values (tuned during impl so structural tests below pass):
  - **flat**: `seaLevel 43`; every biome `{baseHeight: 48, noiseScale: 0}` → perfectly flat dry ground (above sea = no water), biome-colored top.
  - **amplified**: `seaLevel 43`; `GEN` baseHeights, `noiseScale ≈ ×2` (mountains a touch less to limit clamping at `sizeY-5`).
  - **islands**: `seaLevel ≈ 50`; land biomes nudged up so they form **gently-sloped** islands above a raised sea (e.g. Plains 52/3, Forest 54/4, Desert 51/3, Ocean 36/3, Mountains 62/14) — gentle so `findSpawnOnLand`'s ≤2 slope check still finds a dry spawn column.

### 3. Persist the type (game layer)

- `lib/game/worlds.ts`: add `worldType: WorldType` to `WorldMeta`; `sanitizeWorld` coerces
  unknown → `"default"` (via `isWorldType`); `createWorld(profileId, name, seedInput, worldType: WorldType = "default", deps = {})`
  stores it. Add UI metadata `WORLD_TYPE_PRESETS: { id: WorldType; label: string; blurb: string }[]`
  (game/UI layer owns the labels; reuses the `WorldType` ids from `@/lib/world`).
- `lib/game/types.ts`: add optional `worldType?: WorldType` to `SaveData` (additive, **version
  stays 5**, no migration — absent ⇒ default).
- `lib/game/engine/GameEngine.ts`: add `worldType?` to `GameEngineOptions`; in the constructor
  `const worldType = save?.worldType ?? options.worldType ?? "default"` then
  `generateWorld(world, worldType)`; `serialize()` writes `worldType` (mirrors `seed`).
  WorldMeta is authoritative; storing in the blob keeps it self-contained.
- `lib/game/useMinecraftGame.ts`: capture `worldTypeRef = opts.world.worldType` and pass
  `worldType: worldTypeRef.current` alongside the existing `seed: worldSeedRef.current` in
  `attachMount` (line ~150).

### 4. UI (menu layer)

- `components/menu/CreateWorldForm.tsx`: add a **type picker** above the seed field —
  a swatch grid of `WORLD_TYPE_PRESETS` (label + blurb, `aria-pressed` for the selected),
  defaulting to `"default"`, mirroring how `CreateProfileForm` renders the skin grid. Change
  the submit callback to `onCreate(name, seed, worldType)`.
- `components/menu/WorldSelect.tsx`: thread the type into `createWorld(profile.id, name, seed, worldType)`;
  show the type on the world card sub-line for non-default (e.g. `Flat · Seed 1337`).
- `app/menu.css`: a small `.world-type-grid` / `.world-type-option` built on the existing
  `.mc-button` bevel + `aria-pressed` highlight (same pattern as `.skin-swatch`); zero assets.

## Files

**New:** `lib/world/worldTypes.ts` (+ barrel export), `lib/world/worldTypes.test.ts`.
**Modified:** `lib/world/generation.ts` (fork + 3 threaded fns), `lib/world/generation.test.ts`
(new-type hash baselines + structural tests), `lib/game/worlds.ts`, `lib/game/types.ts`,
`lib/game/engine/GameEngine.ts`, `lib/game/useMinecraftGame.ts`, `components/menu/CreateWorldForm.tsx`,
`components/menu/WorldSelect.tsx`, `app/menu.css`, the tests under `components/menu/` and
`lib/game/worlds.test.ts`, plus docs.

**Reuse:** `findSpawnOnLand` (`lib/game/spawn.ts:20` — already rejects water + steep slopes,
which is why Islands must stay gently sloped); the skin-grid swatch pattern in
`CreateProfileForm.tsx`; the existing `GEN` object for all non-terrain passes.

## Determinism / save impact

- **Default path stays byte-identical** — existing world hashes in `generation.test.ts` must
  remain unchanged after the refactor (that's the regression guard). No `WORLDGEN_VERSION` bump.
- Each new type is pinned by its **own** SHA-256 baseline (generated once: temporarily log the
  hash, run, paste — per the docs/testing.md re-baseline policy).
- `worldType` becomes part of the save contract for non-default worlds (the engine must
  regenerate with the same type the diffs were recorded against) — carried on `WorldMeta`
  (authoritative) and in the `SaveData` blob (self-contained, like `seed`). Old worlds /
  legacy-migrated "My World" have no `worldType` ⇒ `"default"` ⇒ correct.

## Verification

- `bun test`:
  - `worldTypes.test.ts` — `isWorldType` membership/fallback.
  - `worlds.test.ts` — `createWorld` stores the type; unknown coerces to default; update the
    existing `createWorld(...)` call sites for the new positional arg.
  - `generation.test.ts` — **default hashes unchanged**; new hash baselines for flat/amplified/islands;
    structural probes: flat surface-height variance ≈ 0; amplified variance > default; islands has a
    materially higher water-column fraction **and** `findSpawnOnLand` returns a column whose floor is
    above sea level and not water (guards the Islands spawn risk).
  - `CreateWorldForm.test.tsx` — picker defaults to Default, selecting a type and submitting passes it
    to `onCreate`; `WorldSelect` forwards it to `createWorld`.
- `bun run test:e2e` — extend `e2e/menu.e2e.ts`: create a **Flat** world, boot it, and sample a few
  surface heights via `window.__monecraft` to assert the terrain near spawn is flat.
- Full gate: `lint`, `typecheck`, `format:check`, `bun test`, `bun run build`, `bun run test:e2e`.
- **Manual pass** (worldgen is visual — see docs/testing.md): eyeball each type once (flat plain,
  amplified peaks, island archipelago with a dry spawn).
- Docs with the change: `save-format.md` (worldType on WorldMeta + SaveData, default byte-identical,
  new baselines), `testing.md` (new hash baselines + structural tests), `tuning.md` (the world-type
  terrain configs), `manual.md` + `reference.md` (choosing a world type), `CHANGELOG.md`.

## Commit slices (Conventional Commits; lint green each step)

1. `feat(worldgen): add Default/Flat/Amplified/Islands world types` — `worldTypes.ts`, `terrainConfigFor`, `generateWorld(world, worldType)` + 3 threaded fns; default byte-identical; new hash + structural tests.
2. `feat(save): persist world type on the world and save blob` — `WorldMeta`/`createWorld`/sanitize + `WORLD_TYPE_PRESETS`, `SaveData.worldType`, engine threading + serialize, `useMinecraftGame` passes it; unit tests.
3. `feat(menu): choose a world type when creating a world` — `CreateWorldForm` picker, `WorldSelect` threading + card label, `menu.css`; component + e2e tests.
4. `docs: document world types` — save-format, testing, tuning, manual, reference, CHANGELOG.

# World Types in New-World Creation

## Context

The new-world form (`components/menu/CreateWorldForm.tsx`, shipped in the worlds & profiles
PR #21) only lets the player set a name and a seed ("leave blank for random"). But the
worldgen produces **one fixed 512×150×512 region with all five biomes baked in by fixed
thresholds** (sea level always 43, mountains always present) — so a different seed only
reshuffles detail; it can't give a flat, amplified, or island world. The player can't
actually choose the *character* of their world.

This adds **world types** to creation — **Default, Superflat, Amplified, Islands** (the
terrain-config-only set; biome-biased types were explicitly excluded). Each is a real
generation variant the player picks alongside name + seed. The type is fixed at creation
(like the seed) and recorded on the world.

**Determinism is preserved.** `generateWorld` forks on the type *before any block write*;
the Default branch uses the existing `GEN` values unchanged, so its output stays
byte-identical and **existing worlds and the current hash tests are untouched** — no
`WORLDGEN_VERSION` bump. Each new type is independently deterministic and gets its own hash
baseline. (Terrain generation reads `smoothNoise2D`/`hash2D`, never the `rand` PRNG, so a
terrain-config change can't desync the default stream — it only changes that type's own
downstream output, which is what we want.)

## Design

### 1. World-type definitions (world layer — `lib/world/`)

New `lib/world/worldTypes.ts` (no `GEN` dependency, so no import cycle):

```ts
export type WorldType = "default" | "flat" | "amplified" | "islands";
export const WORLD_TYPE_IDS: readonly WorldType[] = ["default", "flat", "amplified", "islands"];
export function isWorldType(v: unknown): v is WorldType { /* membership check */ }
```

Export from the `lib/world/index.ts` barrel.

### 2. Terrain config fork (`lib/world/generation.ts`)

- `generateWorld(world)` → **`generateWorld(world, worldType: WorldType = "default")`** (optional
  param ⇒ existing `generateWorld(world)` test calls stay "default" ⇒ byte-identical).
- Add `terrainConfigFor(worldType)` returning `{ seaLevel, biomes: Record<BiomeId, {baseHeight, noiseScale}> }`.
  `"default"` returns exactly `GEN.seaLevel` / `GEN.biomes` values (byte-identical path).
- Thread the config into the **only three** functions that vary; everything else
  (`carveCaves`, `placeOres`, `placeLava`, `placeTrees`, `placeCacti`, `placeStructures`,
  `placeDungeons`) keeps reading `GEN` unchanged:
  - `generateTerrain(world, cfg)` — read `cfg.biomes[biome]` (was `GEN.biomes[biome]`, line 110); keep `GEN.snowAboveY`/`mountainStoneAboveY`/`borderWallHeight`.
  - `placeWater(world, cfg)` — `cfg.seaLevel` (was `GEN.seaLevel`, line 212).
  - `placeBeaches(world, cfg)` — `cfg.seaLevel` (lines 275, 281).
- Starting config values (tuned during impl so structural tests below pass):
  - **flat**: `seaLevel 43`; every biome `{baseHeight: 48, noiseScale: 0}` → perfectly flat dry ground (above sea = no water), biome-colored top.
  - **amplified**: `seaLevel 43`; `GEN` baseHeights, `noiseScale ≈ ×2` (mountains a touch less to limit clamping at `sizeY-5`).
  - **islands**: `seaLevel ≈ 50`; land biomes nudged up so they form **gently-sloped** islands above a raised sea (e.g. Plains 52/3, Forest 54/4, Desert 51/3, Ocean 36/3, Mountains 62/14) — gentle so `findSpawnOnLand`'s ≤2 slope check still finds a dry spawn column.

### 3. Persist the type (game layer)

- `lib/game/worlds.ts`: add `worldType: WorldType` to `WorldMeta`; `sanitizeWorld` coerces
  unknown → `"default"` (via `isWorldType`); `createWorld(profileId, name, seedInput, worldType: WorldType = "default", deps = {})`
  stores it. Add UI metadata `WORLD_TYPE_PRESETS: { id: WorldType; label: string; blurb: string }[]`
  (game/UI layer owns the labels; reuses the `WorldType` ids from `@/lib/world`).
- `lib/game/types.ts`: add optional `worldType?: WorldType` to `SaveData` (additive, **version
  stays 5**, no migration — absent ⇒ default).
- `lib/game/engine/GameEngine.ts`: add `worldType?` to `GameEngineOptions`; in the constructor
  `const worldType = save?.worldType ?? options.worldType ?? "default"` then
  `generateWorld(world, worldType)`; `serialize()` writes `worldType` (mirrors `seed`).
  WorldMeta is authoritative; storing in the blob keeps it self-contained.
- `lib/game/useMinecraftGame.ts`: capture `worldTypeRef = opts.world.worldType` and pass
  `worldType: worldTypeRef.current` alongside the existing `seed: worldSeedRef.current` in
  `attachMount` (line ~150).

### 4. UI (menu layer)

- `components/menu/CreateWorldForm.tsx`: add a **type picker** above the seed field —
  a swatch grid of `WORLD_TYPE_PRESETS` (label + blurb, `aria-pressed` for the selected),
  defaulting to `"default"`, mirroring how `CreateProfileForm` renders the skin grid. Change
  the submit callback to `onCreate(name, seed, worldType)`.
- `components/menu/WorldSelect.tsx`: thread the type into `createWorld(profile.id, name, seed, worldType)`;
  show the type on the world card sub-line for non-default (e.g. `Flat · Seed 1337`).
- `app/menu.css`: a small `.world-type-grid` / `.world-type-option` built on the existing
  `.mc-button` bevel + `aria-pressed` highlight (same pattern as `.skin-swatch`); zero assets.

## Files

**New:** `lib/world/worldTypes.ts` (+ barrel export), `lib/world/worldTypes.test.ts`.
**Modified:** `lib/world/generation.ts` (fork + 3 threaded fns), `lib/world/generation.test.ts`
(new-type hash baselines + structural tests), `lib/game/worlds.ts`, `lib/game/types.ts`,
`lib/game/engine/GameEngine.ts`, `lib/game/useMinecraftGame.ts`, `components/menu/CreateWorldForm.tsx`,
`components/menu/WorldSelect.tsx`, `app/menu.css`, the tests under `components/menu/` and
`lib/game/worlds.test.ts`, plus docs.

**Reuse:** `findSpawnOnLand` (`lib/game/spawn.ts:20` — already rejects water + steep slopes,
which is why Islands must stay gently sloped); the skin-grid swatch pattern in
`CreateProfileForm.tsx`; the existing `GEN` object for all non-terrain passes.

## Determinism / save impact

- **Default path stays byte-identical** — existing world hashes in `generation.test.ts` must
  remain unchanged after the refactor (that's the regression guard). No `WORLDGEN_VERSION` bump.
- Each new type is pinned by its **own** SHA-256 baseline (generated once: temporarily log the
  hash, run, paste — per the docs/testing.md re-baseline policy).
- `worldType` becomes part of the save contract for non-default worlds (the engine must
  regenerate with the same type the diffs were recorded against) — carried on `WorldMeta`
  (authoritative) and in the `SaveData` blob (self-contained, like `seed`). Old worlds /
  legacy-migrated "My World" have no `worldType` ⇒ `"default"` ⇒ correct.

## Verification

- `bun test`:
  - `worldTypes.test.ts` — `isWorldType` membership/fallback.
  - `worlds.test.ts` — `createWorld` stores the type; unknown coerces to default; update the
    existing `createWorld(...)` call sites for the new positional arg.
  - `generation.test.ts` — **default hashes unchanged**; new hash baselines for flat/amplified/islands;
    structural probes: flat surface-height variance ≈ 0; amplified variance > default; islands has a
    materially higher water-column fraction **and** `findSpawnOnLand` returns a column whose floor is
    above sea level and not water (guards the Islands spawn risk).
  - `CreateWorldForm.test.tsx` — picker defaults to Default, selecting a type and submitting passes it
    to `onCreate`; `WorldSelect` forwards it to `createWorld`.
- `bun run test:e2e` — extend `e2e/menu.e2e.ts`: create a **Flat** world, boot it, and sample a few
  surface heights via `window.__monecraft` to assert the terrain near spawn is flat.
- Full gate: `lint`, `typecheck`, `format:check`, `bun test`, `bun run build`, `bun run test:e2e`.
- **Manual pass** (worldgen is visual — see docs/testing.md): eyeball each type once (flat plain,
  amplified peaks, island archipelago with a dry spawn).
- Docs with the change: `save-format.md` (worldType on WorldMeta + SaveData, default byte-identical,
  new baselines), `testing.md` (new hash baselines + structural tests), `tuning.md` (the world-type
  terrain configs), `manual.md` + `reference.md` (choosing a world type), `CHANGELOG.md`.

## Commit slices (Conventional Commits; lint green each step)

1. `feat(worldgen): add Default/Flat/Amplified/Islands world types` — `worldTypes.ts`, `terrainConfigFor`, `generateWorld(world, worldType)` + 3 threaded fns; default byte-identical; new hash + structural tests.
2. `feat(save): persist world type on the world and save blob` — `WorldMeta`/`createWorld`/sanitize + `WORLD_TYPE_PRESETS`, `SaveData.worldType`, engine threading + serialize, `useMinecraftGame` passes it; unit tests.
3. `feat(menu): choose a world type when creating a world` — `CreateWorldForm` picker, `WorldSelect` threading + card label, `menu.css`; component + e2e tests.
4. `docs: document world types` — save-format, testing, tuning, manual, reference, CHANGELOG.

feat(worldgen): add Default/Flat/Amplified/Islands world types

Introduce generation presets the player can pick at world creation. Each
is a terrain-config variant over the same biome map:

- Flat: level dry ground at y=48 (caves still run, so ores stay mineable).
- Amplified: per-biome noise amplitude doubled for dramatic relief.
- Islands: a raised sea (54) with land biomes lifted so they break the
  surface as gently sloped islands while oceans become deep channels.

generateWorld(world, worldType="default") forks on the type up front via
terrainConfigFor() and threads the config into the only three functions
that vary (generateTerrain, placeWater, placeBeaches); caves, ores, lava,
trees, structures, and dungeons still read GEN. The "default" config
returns the GEN values verbatim, so the default world stays
byte-identical — the existing determinism hashes are unchanged and no
WORLDGEN_VERSION bump is needed.

WorldType lives in lib/world/worldTypes.ts (free of GEN so the game layer
can import it without the worldgen module). Each new type is pinned by its
own SHA-256 baseline, plus structural probes: flat concentrates at y=48,
amplified spans a wider height band than default, and islands floods more
of the map while still leaving dry, standable land above the sea.
EOF
